1	"""
2	KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes Art/Models/boss_fixed/publisher_rig.blend).
3	
4	Rebuilds the Publisher's rig from the Meshy files: welds the mesh, refits the Meshy skeleton to the fat body (same bone
5	names and rest orientations, so the Meshy clips still play), adds a root and four helper bones (belly, three jacket
6	flaps), drops the Meshy end bones and paints new skin weights from scratch.
7	
8	    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/build_rig.py
9	
10	The weights are a function of the rest (T-pose) position and of the texture colour, not of bone distance: the trunk
11	follows pelvis and spine by height, the arm starts at the sleeve, the leg below the jacket hem, the head is the skin.
12	"""
13	import colorsys
14	import heapq
15	import math
16	import os
17	
18	import bmesh
19	import bpy
20	import numpy as np
21	from mathutils import Vector, kdtree
22	
23	HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
24	ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", ".."))
25	SRC = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models", "boss_clips", "result.animation_fbx_url.fbx")
26	OUT_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models", "boss_fixed")
27	OUT = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "publisher_rig.blend")
28	
29	END_BONES = ["head_end", "headfront", "LeftHand_End", "RightHand_End", "LeftToe_end", "RightToe_end"]
30	SHOULDER_X, ELBOW_X, WRIST_X = 0.66, 0.92, 1.13
31	KNEE_Z, ANKLE_Z = 0.69, 0.21
32	SPINE_Z = (1.46, 1.68, 1.91)
33	
34	
35	def ss(a, b, x):
36	    """Smoothstep from 0 at a to 1 at b; a may be greater than b."""
37	    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
38	    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
39	
40	
41	def import_source():
42	    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
43	    bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx(filepath=SRC)
44	    arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
45	    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
46	    world = mesh.matrix_world.copy()
47	    mesh.parent = None
48	    mesh.matrix_world = world
49	    for o in (arm, mesh):
50	        o.select_set(True)
51	    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
52	    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=True, rotation=True, scale=True)
53	    mesh.parent = arm
54	    mesh.matrix_parent_inverse.identity()
55	    arm.name = "Armature"
56	    arm.data.name = "PublisherSkeleton"
57	    mesh.name = "SK_Publisher"
58	    mesh.data.name = "SK_Publisher"
59	    return arm, mesh
60	
61	
62	def weld(mesh):
63	    bm = bmesh.new()
64	    bm.from_mesh(mesh.data)
65	    bmesh.ops.remove_doubles(bm, verts=bm.verts, dist=1e-5)
66	    for f in bm.faces:
67	        f.smooth = True
68	    bm.to_mesh(mesh.data)
69	    bm.free()
70	    me = mesh.data
71	    if me.attributes.get("custom_normal"):
72	        me.attributes.remove(me.attributes["custom_normal"])
73	    me.update()
74	
75	
76	def slice_centre(co, lo, hi, axis, side_min=0.02):
77	    """Bounding-box centre of the left-side vertices whose `axis` coordinate is in [lo, hi]."""
78	    m = (co[:, axis] >= lo) & (co[:, axis] <= hi) & (co[:, 0] > side_min)
79	    part = co[m]
80	    return (part.min(axis=0) + part.max(axis=0)) / 2.0
81	
82	
83	def measure(co):
84	    """Joint positions of the left side, from the body itself."""
85	    knee = slice_centre(co, KNEE_Z - 0.04, KNEE_Z + 0.04, 2)
86	    ankle = slice_centre(co, ANKLE_Z, ANKLE_Z + 0.08, 2)
87	    arm = slice_centre(co, 0.82, 1.02, 0)
88	    shoe = co[(co[:, 2] < 0.14) & (co[:, 0] > 0.02)][:, :2]
89	    mean = shoe.mean(axis=0)
90	    _, vecs = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov((shoe - mean).T))
91	    toe_dir = vecs[:, 1]
92	    if toe_dir[1] > 0:
93	        toe_dir = -toe_dir
94	    t = (shoe - mean) @ toe_dir
95	    heel, toe = mean + toe_dir * t.min(), mean + toe_dir * t.max()
96	    ball = heel + (toe - heel) * 0.66
97	    joints = {
98	        "thigh": (0.20, 0.10, 1.08),
99	        "calf": (knee[0], knee[1] - 0.02, KNEE_Z),
100	        "foot": (ankle[0], ankle[1] + 0.03, ANKLE_Z),
101	        "ball": (ball[0], ball[1], 0.05),
102	        "clavicle": (0.09, 0.17, 2.12),
103	        "upperarm": (SHOULDER_X, arm[1], arm[2] + 0.02),
104	        "lowerarm": (ELBOW_X, arm[1], arm[2]),
105	        "hand": (WRIST_X, arm[1], arm[2]),
106	    }
107	    print("[build] toe_dir", toe_dir, "heel", heel, "toe", toe)
108	    for k, v in joints.items():
109	        print("[build] joint %-9s %.3f %.3f %.3f" % (k, *v))
110	    return joints, toe_dir, np.array(joints["ball"][:2])
111	
112	
113	def refit_skeleton(arm, joints):
114	    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
115	    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="EDIT")
116	    eb = arm.data.edit_bones
117	    for b in eb:
118	        b.use_connect = False
119	    for name in END_BONES:
120	        eb.remove(eb[name])
121	
122	    def move(name, head):
123	        b = eb[name]
124	        d = Vector(head) - b.head
125	        b.head += d
126	        b.tail += d
127	
128	    centre = {"pelvis": (0, 0.08, 1.20), "spine_01": (0, 0.10, SPINE_Z[0]), "spine_02": (0, 0.125, SPINE_Z[1]),
129	              "spine_03": (0, 0.15, SPINE_Z[2]), "neck_01": (0, 0.17, 2.10), "head": (0, 0.16, 2.20)}
130	    for name, head in centre.items():
131	        move(name, head)
132	    for key, (x, y, z) in joints.items():
133	        move(key + "_l", (x, y, z))
134	        move(key + "_r", (-x, y, z))
135	
136	    def helper(name, head, parent):
137	        b = eb.new(name)
138	        b.head = Vector(head)
139	        b.tail = Vector(head) + Vector((0, 0.2, 0))
140	        b.roll = 0.0
141	        b.parent = eb[parent] if parent else None
142	        b.use_deform = True
143	        return b
144	
145	    root = helper("root", (0, 0, 0), None)
146	    eb["pelvis"].parent = root
147	    helper("belly", (0, -0.10, 1.48), "spine_01")
148	    helper("jacket_front_l", (0.36, -0.38, 1.52), "spine_01")
149	    helper("jacket_front_r", (-0.36, -0.38, 1.52), "spine_01")
150	    helper("jacket_back", (0, 0.50, 1.52), "pelvis")
151	    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")
152	
153	
154	def vertex_colours(mesh):
155	    """Mean base-colour of each vertex, sampled through its UVs."""
156	    me = mesh.data
157	    image = None
158	    for mat in me.materials:
159	        if mat and mat.use_nodes:
160	            for node in mat.node_tree.nodes:
161	                if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
162	                    link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
163	                    if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
164	                        image = link[0].from_node.image
165	    if image is None:
166	        image = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.size[0] > 0)
167	    w, h = image.size
168	    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
169	    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
170	    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
171	    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2)
172	    vi = np.zeros(len(me.loops), dtype=np.int64)
173	    me.loops.foreach_get("vertex_index", vi)
174	    xs = np.clip((uv[:, 0] % 1.0 * w).astype(int), 0, w - 1)
175	    ys = np.clip((uv[:, 1] % 1.0 * h).astype(int), 0, h - 1)
176	    rgb = px[ys, xs, :3]
177	    total = np.zeros((len(me.vertices), 3))
178	    count = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
179	    np.add.at(total, vi, rgb)
180	    np.add.at(count, vi, 1)
181	    return total / np.maximum(count, 1)[:, None]
182	
183	
184	def neighbours(me):
185	    adj = [[] for _ in me.vertices]
186	    for e in me.edges:
187	        a, b = e.vertices
188	        adj[a].append(b)
189	        adj[b].append(a)
190	    return adj
191	
192	
193	def geodesic(co, adj, sources, limit):
194	    dist = np.full(len(co), np.inf)
195	    heap = []
196	    for s in sources:
197	        dist[s] = 0.0
198	        heap.append((0.0, int(s)))
199	    heapq.heapify(heap)
200	    while heap:
201	        d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
202	        if d > dist[a] or d > limit:
203	            continue
204	        for b in adj[a]:
205	            nd = d + float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b]))
206	            if nd < dist[b]:
207	                dist[b] = nd
208	                heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
209	    return dist
210	
211	
212	def head_set(co, rgb, adj):
213	    hsv = np.array([colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*c) for c in rgb])
214	    black = hsv[:, 2] < 0.18
215	    cream = (hsv[:, 1] < 0.28) & (hsv[:, 2] > 0.45)
216	    x, z = np.abs(co[:, 0]), co[:, 2]
217	    head = ((~black & ~cream) & (z > 2.13) & (x < 0.36)) | (z > 2.44)
218	    # Shaded creases of the collar and the lapels pass the colour test too: only what is joined to the skull through
219	    # skin is the head, otherwise the lapel tips follow the head and lift off the jacket.
220	    reached = np.zeros(len(co), dtype=bool)
221	    stack = [int(i) for i in np.where(z > 2.44)[0]]
222	    reached[stack] = True
223	    while stack:
224	        a = stack.pop()
225	        for b in adj[a]:
226	            if head[b] and not reached[b]:
227	                reached[b] = True
228	                stack.append(b)
229	    print("[build] head candidates %d, joined to the skull %d" % (head.sum(), reached.sum()))
230	    head = reached
231	    # Teeth, eyes and the top-knot: whatever is cut off from the body by the skin is the head too.
232	    seen = head.copy()
233	    for start in np.where(~head)[0]:
234	        if seen[start]:
235	            continue
236	        comp, stack, low = [start], [start], False
237	        seen[start] = True
238	        while stack:
239	            a = stack.pop()
240	            if co[a, 2] < 2.0:
241	                low = True
242	            for b in adj[a]:
243	                if not seen[b]:
244	                    seen[b] = True
245	                    comp.append(b)
246	                    stack.append(b)
247	        if not low:
248	            head[comp] = True
249	    return head, black, cream, hsv
250	
251	
252	def paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy):
253	    me = mesh.data
254	    n = len(me.vertices)
255	    co = np.zeros(n * 3)
256	    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
257	    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
258	    x, y, z = co[:, 0], co[:, 1], co[:, 2]
259	    ax = np.abs(x)
260	    adj = neighbours(me)
261	    rgb = vertex_colours(mesh)
262	    head, black, cream, hsv = head_set(co, rgb, adj)
263	    red = ((hsv[:, 0] < 0.03) | (hsv[:, 0] > 0.95)) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.6)
264	    print("[build] head verts %d, black %d, cream %d" % (head.sum(), black.sum(), cream.sum()))
265	
266	    names = [b.name for b in arm.data.bones]
267	    w = {name: np.zeros(n) for name in names}
268	
269	    # Trunk: a partition by height.
270	    h = 0.14
271	    s1, s2, s3 = (ss(c - h, c + h, z) for c in SPINE_Z)
272	    w["pelvis"] = 1 - s1
273	    w["spine_01"] = s1 * (1 - s2)
274	    w["spine_02"] = s2 * (1 - s3)
275	    w["spine_03"] = s3
276	    trunk = ["pelvis", "spine_01", "spine_02", "spine_03"]
277	
278	    def scale(keys, factor):
279	        for k in keys:
280	            w[k] = w[k] * factor
281	
282	    # Belly: the front bulge, shirt and jacket front alike.
283	    belly = 0.75 * ss(0.08, -0.30, y) * ss(1.95, 1.58, z) * ss(0.98, 1.14, z) * ss(0.72, 0.42, ax)
284	    scale(trunk, 1 - belly)
285	    w["belly"] = belly
286	
287	    # Jacket flaps: the cream skirt of the jacket from the hem up to the waist.
288	    jacket = (~black & ~red & (z > 1.15)).astype(float)
289	    flap = 0.85 * ss(1.50, 1.24, z) * jacket
290	    theta = np.abs(np.arctan2(x, -y))
291	    back = ss(math.radians(80), math.radians(120), theta)
292	    scale(trunk + ["belly"], 1 - flap)
293	    w["jacket_back"] = flap * back
294	    w["jacket_front_l"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x > 0)
295	    w["jacket_front_r"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x <= 0)
296	    body = trunk + ["belly", "jacket_back", "jacket_front_l", "jacket_front_r"]
297	
298	    # Legs: below a hip line that runs from the crotch up to the outside of the hip, never into the jacket.
299	    zc = 0.90 + 0.17 * ss(0.0, 0.35, ax)
300	    leg = ss(zc + 0.13, zc - 0.13, z)
301	    leg = np.where(black & (z > 0.9), 0.0, leg)
302	    leg = np.where(z > 1.165, 0.0, leg)
303	    scale(body, 1 - leg)
304	    left = ss(-0.05, 0.05, x)
305	    knee = ss(KNEE_Z + 0.10, KNEE_Z - 0.10, z)
306	    foot = ss(0.27, 0.15, z)
307	    for side, share, sx in (("l", left, 1.0), ("r", 1 - left, -1.0)):
308	        t = (x * sx - ball_xy[0]) * toe_dir[0] + (y - ball_xy[1]) * toe_dir[1]
309	        toe = ss(-0.04, 0.04, t) * ss(0.16, 0.10, z)
310	        w["thigh_" + side] = leg * share * (1 - knee)
311	        w["calf_" + side] = leg * share * knee * (1 - foot)
312	        w["foot_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * (1 - toe)
313	        w["ball_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * toe
314	
315	    # Arms: the sleeve from the shoulder seam outwards; the jacket under the armpit stays on the spine.
316	    gate = ss(1.80, 1.93, z)
317	    arm_m = ss(0.60, 0.82, ax) * gate
318	    clav = 0.6 * ss(0.14, 0.42, ax) * ss(1.88, 2.08, z) * (1 - arm_m)
319	    scale(body, 1 - arm_m - clav)
320	    elbow = ss(ELBOW_X - 0.07, ELBOW_X + 0.07, ax)
321	    wrist = ss(WRIST_X - 0.04, WRIST_X + 0.04, ax)
322	    for side, m in (("l", x > 0), ("r", x <= 0)):
323	        w["clavicle_" + side] = clav * m
324	        w["upperarm_" + side] = arm_m * (1 - elbow) * m
325	        w["lowerarm_" + side] = arm_m * elbow * (1 - wrist) * m
326	        w["hand_" + side] = arm_m * wrist * m
327	
328	    # Head and neck: the skin is the head; the twist is spread over the jowls and a short ring of the collar.
329	    out = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(head)[0], 0.4)
330	    inside = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(~head)[0], 0.4)
331	    hn = np.where(head, 1.0, 1 - ss(0.0, 0.12, out))
332	    w_head = np.where(head, 0.6 + 0.4 * ss(0.0, 0.10, inside), 0.6 * (1 - ss(0.0, 0.07, out)))
333	    for k in names:
334	        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hn)
335	    w["head"] = w_head
336	    w["neck_01"] = np.maximum(hn - w_head, 0.0)
337	
338	    W = np.stack([w[k] for k in names], axis=1)
339	    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
340	
341	    # Smooth over the surface, then put the rigid parts back.
342	    rigid = (head & (inside > 0.08)) | (ax > WRIST_X + 0.08) | (z < 0.12)
343	    fixed = W.copy()
344	    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
345	    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
346	    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
347	    for _ in range(6):
348	        avg = np.zeros_like(W)
349	        np.add.at(avg, idx, W[nbr])
350	        avg /= deg[:, None]
351	        W = 0.5 * W + 0.5 * avg
352	        W[rigid] = fixed[rigid]
353	
354	    # Layers that lie on each other (lapel on jacket, jacket edge on shirt, tie on shirt) are not neighbours on the
355	    # surface, so the smoothing drives them apart: average the torso over space as well.
356	    layered = np.where(~head & (z > 1.15) & (ax < ELBOW_X))[0]
357	    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(layered))
358	    for k, i in enumerate(layered):
359	        tree.insert(co[i], k)
360	    tree.balance()
361	    near = [[layered[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_range(co[i], 0.03)] for i in layered]
362	    for _ in range(3):
363	        W[layered] = np.array([W[group].mean(axis=0) for group in near])
364	
365	    # At most four influences, normalised.
366	    order = np.argsort(-W, axis=1)
367	    keep = np.zeros_like(W, dtype=bool)
368	    np.put_along_axis(keep, order[:, :4], True, axis=1)
369	    W = np.where(keep & (W > 0.01), W, 0.0)
370	    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
371	
372	    mesh.vertex_groups.clear()
373	    for j, name in enumerate(names):
374	        g = mesh.vertex_groups.new(name=name)
375	        col = W[:, j]
376	        for i in np.where(col > 0)[0]:
377	            g.add([int(i)], float(col[i]), "REPLACE")
378	    used = (W > 0).sum(axis=1)
379	    print("[build] influences per vertex: max %d, mean %.2f" % (used.max(), used.mean()))
380	    for j, name in enumerate(names):
381	        print("[build] group %-16s verts=%5d weight=%8.1f" % (name, (W[:, j] > 0).sum(), W[:, j].sum()))
382	
383	
384	def clean_actions(arm):
385	    """Meshy names are 'Armature|Idle'; curves of the dropped bones and of the armature object itself go."""
386	    bones = {b.name for b in arm.data.bones}
387	    for action in list(bpy.data.actions):
388	        action.name = action.name.split("|")[-1]
389	        removed = 0
390	        for layer in action.layers:
391	            for strip in layer.strips:
392	                for slot in action.slots:
393	                    bag = strip.channelbag(slot)
394	                    if bag is None:
395	                        continue
396	                    for fc in list(bag.fcurves):
397	                        path = fc.data_path
398	                        name = path.split('"')[1] if path.startswith("pose.bones[") else None
399	                        if name is None or name not in bones:
400	                            bag.fcurves.remove(fc)
401	                            removed += 1
402	        action.use_fake_user = True
403	        print("[build] action %-22s frames %s, dropped %d curves" % (action.name, tuple(action.frame_range), removed))
404	
405	
406	def main():
407	    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
408	    arm, mesh = import_source()
409	    weld(mesh)
410	    me = mesh.data
411	    co = np.zeros(len(me.vertices) * 3)
412	    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
413	    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
414	    print("[build] welded verts %d, bbox %s %s" % (len(co), co.min(axis=0).round(3), co.max(axis=0).round(3)))
415	    joints, toe_dir, ball_xy = measure(co)
416	    refit_skeleton(arm, joints)
417	    paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy)
418	    clean_actions(arm)
419	    # The Meshy clips keyed the armature object itself at 90 degrees; with those curves gone it stays upright.
420	    arm.animation_data.action = None
421	    arm.location = (0, 0, 0)
422	    arm.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)
423	    arm.rotation_quaternion = (1, 0, 0, 0)
424	    arm.scale = (1, 1, 1)
425	    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
426	        pb.matrix_basis.identity()
427	    bpy.context.scene.render.fps = 30
428	    try:
429	        bpy.ops.file.pack_all()
430	    except RuntimeError as e:
431	        print("[build] pack_all:", e)
432	    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=OUT)
433	    print("[build] saved", OUT)
434	
435	
436	main()

"""
KIND: offline tool (headless Blender, writes Art/Models/boss_fixed/publisher_rig.blend).

Rebuilds the Publisher's rig from the Meshy files: welds the mesh, refits the Meshy skeleton to the fat body (same bone
names and rest orientations, so the Meshy clips still play), adds a root and four helper bones (belly, three jacket
flaps), drops the Meshy end bones and paints new skin weights from scratch.

    blender -b --factory-startup --python Tools/Art/publisher_rig/build_rig.py

The weights are a function of the rest (T-pose) position and of the texture colour, not of bone distance: the trunk
follows pelvis and spine by height, the arm starts at the sleeve, the leg below the jacket hem, the head is the skin.
"""
import colorsys
import heapq
import math
import os

import bmesh
import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector, kdtree

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", ".."))
SRC = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models", "boss_clips", "result.animation_fbx_url.fbx")
OUT_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "Art", "Models", "boss_fixed")
OUT = os.path.join(OUT_DIR, "publisher_rig.blend")

END_BONES = ["head_end", "headfront", "LeftHand_End", "RightHand_End", "LeftToe_end", "RightToe_end"]
SHOULDER_X, ELBOW_X, WRIST_X = 0.66, 0.92, 1.13
KNEE_Z, ANKLE_Z = 0.69, 0.21
SPINE_Z = (1.46, 1.68, 1.91)


def ss(a, b, x):
    """Smoothstep from 0 at a to 1 at b; a may be greater than b."""
    t = np.clip((x - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)


def import_source():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx(filepath=SRC)
    arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    world = mesh.matrix_world.copy()
    mesh.parent = None
    mesh.matrix_world = world
    for o in (arm, mesh):
        o.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.transform_apply(location=True, rotation=True, scale=True)
    mesh.parent = arm
    mesh.matrix_parent_inverse.identity()
    arm.name = "Armature"
    arm.data.name = "PublisherSkeleton"
    mesh.name = "SK_Publisher"
    mesh.data.name = "SK_Publisher"
    return arm, mesh


def weld(mesh):
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(mesh.data)
    bmesh.ops.remove_doubles(bm, verts=bm.verts, dist=1e-5)
    for f in bm.faces:
        f.smooth = True
    bm.to_mesh(mesh.data)
    bm.free()
    me = mesh.data
    if me.attributes.get("custom_normal"):
        me.attributes.remove(me.attributes["custom_normal"])
    me.update()


def slice_centre(co, lo, hi, axis, side_min=0.02):
    """Bounding-box centre of the left-side vertices whose `axis` coordinate is in [lo, hi]."""
    m = (co[:, axis] >= lo) & (co[:, axis] <= hi) & (co[:, 0] > side_min)
    part = co[m]
    return (part.min(axis=0) + part.max(axis=0)) / 2.0


def measure(co):
    """Joint positions of the left side, from the body itself."""
    knee = slice_centre(co, KNEE_Z - 0.04, KNEE_Z + 0.04, 2)
    ankle = slice_centre(co, ANKLE_Z, ANKLE_Z + 0.08, 2)
    arm = slice_centre(co, 0.82, 1.02, 0)
    shoe = co[(co[:, 2] < 0.14) & (co[:, 0] > 0.02)][:, :2]
    mean = shoe.mean(axis=0)
    _, vecs = np.linalg.eigh(np.cov((shoe - mean).T))
    toe_dir = vecs[:, 1]
    if toe_dir[1] > 0:
        toe_dir = -toe_dir
    t = (shoe - mean) @ toe_dir
    heel, toe = mean + toe_dir * t.min(), mean + toe_dir * t.max()
    ball = heel + (toe - heel) * 0.66
    joints = {
        "thigh": (0.20, 0.10, 1.08),
        "calf": (knee[0], knee[1] - 0.02, KNEE_Z),
        "foot": (ankle[0], ankle[1] + 0.03, ANKLE_Z),
        "ball": (ball[0], ball[1], 0.05),
        "clavicle": (0.09, 0.17, 2.12),
        "upperarm": (SHOULDER_X, arm[1], arm[2] + 0.02),
        "lowerarm": (ELBOW_X, arm[1], arm[2]),
        "hand": (WRIST_X, arm[1], arm[2]),
    }
    print("[build] toe_dir", toe_dir, "heel", heel, "toe", toe)
    for k, v in joints.items():
        print("[build] joint %-9s %.3f %.3f %.3f" % (k, *v))
    return joints, toe_dir, np.array(joints["ball"][:2])


def refit_skeleton(arm, joints):
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = arm
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="EDIT")
    eb = arm.data.edit_bones
    for b in eb:
        b.use_connect = False
    for name in END_BONES:
        eb.remove(eb[name])

    def move(name, head):
        b = eb[name]
        d = Vector(head) - b.head
        b.head += d
        b.tail += d

    centre = {"pelvis": (0, 0.08, 1.20), "spine_01": (0, 0.10, SPINE_Z[0]), "spine_02": (0, 0.125, SPINE_Z[1]),
              "spine_03": (0, 0.15, SPINE_Z[2]), "neck_01": (0, 0.17, 2.10), "head": (0, 0.16, 2.20)}
    for name, head in centre.items():
        move(name, head)
    for key, (x, y, z) in joints.items():
        move(key + "_l", (x, y, z))
        move(key + "_r", (-x, y, z))

    def helper(name, head, parent):
        b = eb.new(name)
        b.head = Vector(head)
        b.tail = Vector(head) + Vector((0, 0.2, 0))
        b.roll = 0.0
        b.parent = eb[parent] if parent else None
        b.use_deform = True
        return b

    root = helper("root", (0, 0, 0), None)
    eb["pelvis"].parent = root
    helper("belly", (0, -0.10, 1.48), "spine_01")
    helper("jacket_front_l", (0.36, -0.38, 1.52), "spine_01")
    helper("jacket_front_r", (-0.36, -0.38, 1.52), "spine_01")
    helper("jacket_back", (0, 0.50, 1.52), "pelvis")
    bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT")


def vertex_colours(mesh):
    """Mean base-colour of each vertex, sampled through its UVs."""
    me = mesh.data
    image = None
    for mat in me.materials:
        if mat and mat.use_nodes:
            for node in mat.node_tree.nodes:

                    link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
                    if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                        image = link[0].from_node.image
    if image is None:
        image = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.size[0] > 0)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2)
    vi = np.zeros(len(me.loops), dtype=np.int64)
    me.loops.foreach_get("vertex_index", vi)
    xs = np.clip((uv[:, 0] % 1.0 * w).astype(int), 0, w - 1)
    ys = np.clip((uv[:, 1] % 1.0 * h).astype(int), 0, h - 1)
    rgb = px[ys, xs, :3]
    total = np.zeros((len(me.vertices), 3))
    count = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
    np.add.at(total, vi, rgb)
    np.add.at(count, vi, 1)
    return total / np.maximum(count, 1)[:, None]


def neighbours(me):
    adj = [[] for _ in me.vertices]
    for e in me.edges:
        a, b = e.vertices
        adj[a].append(b)
        adj[b].append(a)
    return adj


def geodesic(co, adj, sources, limit):
    dist = np.full(len(co), np.inf)
    heap = []
    for s in sources:
        dist[s] = 0.0
        heap.append((0.0, int(s)))
    heapq.heapify(heap)
    while heap:
        d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if d > dist[a] or d > limit:
            continue
        for b in adj[a]:
            nd = d + float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b]))
            if nd < dist[b]:
                dist[b] = nd
                heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
    return dist


def head_set(co, rgb, adj):
    hsv = np.array([colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*c) for c in rgb])
    black = hsv[:, 2] < 0.18
    cream = (hsv[:, 1] < 0.28) & (hsv[:, 2] > 0.45)
    x, z = np.abs(co[:, 0]), co[:, 2]
    head = ((~black & ~cream) & (z > 2.13) & (x < 0.36)) | (z > 2.44)
    # Shaded creases of the collar and the lapels pass the colour test too: only what is joined to the skull through
    # skin is the head, otherwise the lapel tips follow the head and lift off the jacket.
    reached = np.zeros(len(co), dtype=bool)
    stack = [int(i) for i in np.where(z > 2.44)[0]]
    reached[stack] = True
    while stack:
        a = stack.pop()
        for b in adj[a]:
            if head[b] and not reached[b]:
                reached[b] = True
                stack.append(b)
    print("[build] head candidates %d, joined to the skull %d" % (head.sum(), reached.sum()))
    head = reached
    # Teeth, eyes and the top-knot: whatever is cut off from the body by the skin is the head too.
    seen = head.copy()
    for start in np.where(~head)[0]:
        if seen[start]:
            continue
        comp, stack, low = [start], [start], False
        seen[start] = True
        while stack:
            a = stack.pop()
            if co[a, 2] < 2.0:
                low = True
            for b in adj[a]:
                if not seen[b]:
                    seen[b] = True
                    comp.append(b)
                    stack.append(b)
        if not low:
            head[comp] = True
    return head, black, cream, hsv


def paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy):
    me = mesh.data
    n = len(me.vertices)
    co = np.zeros(n * 3)
    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
    x, y, z = co[:, 0], co[:, 1], co[:, 2]
    ax = np.abs(x)
    adj = neighbours(me)
    rgb = vertex_colours(mesh)
    head, black, cream, hsv = head_set(co, rgb, adj)
    red = ((hsv[:, 0] < 0.03) | (hsv[:, 0] > 0.95)) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.6)
    print("[build] head verts %d, black %d, cream %d" % (head.sum(), black.sum(), cream.sum()))

    names = [b.name for b in arm.data.bones]
    w = {name: np.zeros(n) for name in names}

    # Trunk: a partition by height.
    h = 0.14
    s1, s2, s3 = (ss(c - h, c + h, z) for c in SPINE_Z)
    w["pelvis"] = 1 - s1
    w["spine_01"] = s1 * (1 - s2)
    w["spine_02"] = s2 * (1 - s3)
    w["spine_03"] = s3
    trunk = ["pelvis", "spine_01", "spine_02", "spine_03"]

    def scale(keys, factor):
        for k in keys:
            w[k] = w[k] * factor

    # Belly: the front bulge, shirt and jacket front alike.
    belly = 0.75 * ss(0.08, -0.30, y) * ss(1.95, 1.58, z) * ss(0.98, 1.14, z) * ss(0.72, 0.42, ax)
    scale(trunk, 1 - belly)
    w["belly"] = belly

    # Jacket flaps: the cream skirt of the jacket from the hem up to the waist.
    jacket = (~black & ~red & (z > 1.15)).astype(float)
    flap = 0.85 * ss(1.50, 1.24, z) * jacket
    theta = np.abs(np.arctan2(x, -y))
    back = ss(math.radians(80), math.radians(120), theta)
    scale(trunk + ["belly"], 1 - flap)
    w["jacket_back"] = flap * back
    w["jacket_front_l"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x > 0)
    w["jacket_front_r"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x <= 0)
    body = trunk + ["belly", "jacket_back", "jacket_front_l", "jacket_front_r"]

    # Legs: below a hip line that runs from the crotch up to the outside of the hip, never into the jacket.
    zc = 0.90 + 0.17 * ss(0.0, 0.35, ax)
    leg = ss(zc + 0.13, zc - 0.13, z)
    leg = np.where(black & (z > 0.9), 0.0, leg)
    leg = np.where(z > 1.165, 0.0, leg)
    scale(body, 1 - leg)
    left = ss(-0.05, 0.05, x)
    knee = ss(KNEE_Z + 0.10, KNEE_Z - 0.10, z)
    foot = ss(0.27, 0.15, z)
    for side, share, sx in (("l", left, 1.0), ("r", 1 - left, -1.0)):
        t = (x * sx - ball_xy[0]) * toe_dir[0] + (y - ball_xy[1]) * toe_dir[1]
        toe = ss(-0.04, 0.04, t) * ss(0.16, 0.10, z)
        w["thigh_" + side] = leg * share * (1 - knee)
        w["calf_" + side] = leg * share * knee * (1 - foot)
        w["foot_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * (1 - toe)
        w["ball_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * toe

    # Arms: the sleeve from the shoulder seam outwards; the jacket under the armpit stays on the spine.
    gate = ss(1.80, 1.93, z)
    arm_m = ss(0.60, 0.82, ax) * gate
    clav = 0.6 * ss(0.14, 0.42, ax) * ss(1.88, 2.08, z) * (1 - arm_m)
    scale(body, 1 - arm_m - clav)
    elbow = ss(ELBOW_X - 0.07, ELBOW_X + 0.07, ax)
    wrist = ss(WRIST_X - 0.04, WRIST_X + 0.04, ax)
    for side, m in (("l", x > 0), ("r", x <= 0)):
        w["clavicle_" + side] = clav * m
        w["upperarm_" + side] = arm_m * (1 - elbow) * m
        w["lowerarm_" + side] = arm_m * elbow * (1 - wrist) * m
        w["hand_" + side] = arm_m * wrist * m

    # Head and neck: the skin is the head; the twist is spread over the jowls and a short ring of the collar.
    out = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(head)[0], 0.4)
    inside = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(~head)[0], 0.4)
    hn = np.where(head, 1.0, 1 - ss(0.0, 0.12, out))
    w_head = np.where(head, 0.6 + 0.4 * ss(0.0, 0.10, inside), 0.6 * (1 - ss(0.0, 0.07, out)))
    for k in names:
        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hn)
    w["head"] = w_head
    w["neck_01"] = np.maximum(hn - w_head, 0.0)

    W = np.stack([w[k] for k in names], axis=1)
    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

    # Smooth over the surface, then put the rigid parts back.
    rigid = (head & (inside > 0.08)) | (ax > WRIST_X + 0.08) | (z < 0.12)
    fixed = W.copy()
    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
    for _ in range(6):
        avg = np.zeros_like(W)
        np.add.at(avg, idx, W[nbr])
        avg /= deg[:, None]
        W = 0.5 * W + 0.5 * avg
        W[rigid] = fixed[rigid]

    # Layers that lie on each other (lapel on jacket, jacket edge on shirt, tie on shirt) are not neighbours on the
    # surface, so the smoothing drives them apart: average the torso over space as well.
    layered = np.where(~head & (z > 1.15) & (ax < ELBOW_X))[0]
    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(layered))
    for k, i in enumerate(layered):
        tree.insert(co[i], k)
    tree.balance()
    near = [[layered[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_range(co[i], 0.03)] for i in layered]
    for _ in range(3):
        W[layered] = np.array([W[group].mean(axis=0) for group in near])

    # At most four influences, normalised.
    order = np.argsort(-W, axis=1)
    keep = np.zeros_like(W, dtype=bool)
    np.put_along_axis(keep, order[:, :4], True, axis=1)
    W = np.where(keep & (W > 0.01), W, 0.0)
    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

    mesh.vertex_groups.clear()
    for j, name in enumerate(names):
        g = mesh.vertex_groups.new(name=name)
        col = W[:, j]
        for i in np.where(col > 0)[0]:
            g.add([int(i)], float(col[i]), "REPLACE")
    used = (W > 0).sum(axis=1)
    print("[build] influences per vertex: max %d, mean %.2f" % (used.max(), used.mean()))
    for j, name in enumerate(names):
        print("[build] group %-16s verts=%5d weight=%8.1f" % (name, (W[:, j] > 0).sum(), W[:, j].sum()))


def clean_actions(arm):
    """Meshy names are 'Armature|Idle'; curves of the dropped bones and of the armature object itself go."""
    bones = {b.name for b in arm.data.bones}
    for action in list(bpy.data.actions):
        action.name = action.name.split("|")[-1]
        removed = 0
        for layer in action.layers:
            for strip in layer.strips:
                for slot in action.slots:
                    bag = strip.channelbag(slot)
                    if bag is None:
                        continue
                    for fc in list(bag.fcurves):
                        path = fc.data_path
                        name = path.split('"')[1] if path.startswith("pose.bones[") else None
                        if name is None or name not in bones:
                            bag.fcurves.remove(fc)
                            removed += 1
        action.use_fake_user = True
        print("[build] action %-22s frames %s, dropped %d curves" % (action.name, tuple(action.frame_range), removed))


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    arm, mesh = import_source()
    weld(mesh)
    me = mesh.data
    co = np.zeros(len(me.vertices) * 3)
    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
    print("[build] welded verts %d, bbox %s %s" % (len(co), co.min(axis=0).round(3), co.max(axis=0).round(3)))
    joints, toe_dir, ball_xy = measure(co)
    refit_skeleton(arm, joints)
    paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy)
    clean_actions(arm)
    # The Meshy clips keyed the armature object itself at 90 degrees; with those curves gone it stays upright.
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    arm.location = (0, 0, 0)
    arm.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)
    arm.rotation_quaternion = (1, 0, 0, 0)
    arm.scale = (1, 1, 1)
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:
        pb.matrix_basis.identity()
    bpy.context.scene.render.fps = 30
    try:
        bpy.ops.file.pack_all()
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print("[build] pack_all:", e)
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=OUT)
    print("[build] saved", OUT)


main()

import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np


def vertex_colours(mesh):
    me = mesh.data
    image = next(i for i in bpy.data.images if i.size[0] > 0)
    for mat in me.materials:
        if mat and mat.use_nodes:
            for node in mat.node_tree.nodes:
                if node.type == "BSDF_PRINCIPLED":
                    link = node.inputs["Base Color"].links
                    if link and link[0].from_node.type == "TEX_IMAGE":
                        image = link[0].from_node.image
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2)
    vi = np.zeros(len(me.loops), dtype=np.int64)
    me.loops.foreach_get("vertex_index", vi)
    xs = np.clip((uv[:, 0] % 1.0 * w).astype(int), 0, w - 1)
    ys = np.clip((uv[:, 1] % 1.0 * h).astype(int), 0, h - 1)
    total = np.zeros((len(me.vertices), 3))
    count = np.zeros(len(me.vertices))
    np.add.at(total, vi, px[ys, xs, :3])
    np.add.at(count, vi, 1)
    return total / np.maximum(count, 1)[:, None]


def main():
    args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
    bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=args[0])
    mesh = next(o for o in bpy.context.scene.objects if o.type == "MESH")
    me = mesh.data
    co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices])
    hsv = np.array([colorsys.rgb_to_hsv(*c) for c in vertex_colours(mesh)])
    gold = (hsv[:, 0] > 0.07) & (hsv[:, 0] < 0.17) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.45) & (hsv[:, 2] > 0.3)
    zone = (np.abs(co[:, 0]) < 0.32) & (co[:, 1] < 0.0) & (co[:, 2] > 1.2) & (co[:, 2] < 2.15)
    cand = gold & zone
    adj = [[] for _ in me.vertices]
    for e in me.edges:
        a, b = e.vertices
        adj[a].append(b)
        adj[b].append(a)
    lines = ["gold verts in the chest zone: %d" % cand.sum()]
    seen = np.zeros(len(co), dtype=bool)
    parts = []
    for start in np.where(cand)[0]:
        if seen[start]:
            continue
        comp, stack = [start], [start]
        seen[start] = True
        while stack:
            a = stack.pop()
            for b in adj[a]:
                if cand[b] and not seen[b]:
                    seen[b] = True
                    comp.append(b)
                    stack.append(b)
        parts.append(np.array(comp))
    parts.sort(key=len, reverse=True)
    for part in parts[:8]:
        p = co[part]
        border = sum(1 for a in part for b in adj[a] if not cand[b])
        lines.append("part %5d verts  x %.3f..%.3f  y %.3f..%.3f  z %.3f..%.3f  edges to non-gold %d" % (
            len(part), p[:, 0].min(), p[:, 0].max(), p[:, 1].min(), p[:, 1].max(), p[:, 2].min(), p[:, 2].max(),
            border))
    tie = parts[0]
    p = co[tie]
    lines.append("tie centre line (z band: n, x mean, x min..max, y min..max; nearest non-gold y at that x,z)")
    other = np.where(~cand & (co[:, 1] < 0.1))[0]
    for z0 in np.arange(p[:, 2].min(), p[:, 2].max(), 0.04):
        m = (p[:, 2] >= z0) & (p[:, 2] < z0 + 0.04)
        if not m.any():
            continue
        q = p[m]
        cx = q[:, 0].mean()
        near = other[(np.abs(co[other, 0] - cx) < 0.05) & (np.abs(co[other, 2] - z0 - 0.02) < 0.03)]
        shirt = co[near, 1].min() if len(near) else float("nan")
        lines.append("  z %.2f: %4d  x %6.3f  %6.3f..%6.3f  y %6.3f..%6.3f  shirt y %6.3f" % (
            z0, m.sum(), cx, q[:, 0].min(), q[:, 0].max(), q[:, 1].min(), q[:, 1].max(), shirt))
    names = [g.name for g in mesh.vertex_groups]
    total = {}
    for i in tie:
        for g in me.vertices[int(i)].groups:
            total[names[g.group]] = total.get(names[g.group], 0.0) + g.weight
    lines.append("tie weights: " + ", ".join("%s %.0f" % kv for kv in sorted(total.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])))
    with open(args[1], "w") as out:
        out.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


main()

def smooth01(a, b, x):
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, (x - a) / (b - a)))
    return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)


def about(point, axis, angle):
    return Matrix.Translation(point) @ Matrix.Rotation(angle, 4, axis) @ Matrix.Translation(-point)


def relax_raised_hands(world, rest, n, loop, log):
    """A raised arm turns its palm forward and keeps the hand in line with the forearm.

    The turn is shared by the whole arm (about the shoulder-wrist line, so the wrist stays in place), the forearm and
    the hand; the bend of the wrist is cut down to WRIST_BEND while the arm is up.
    """
    forward = Vector((0.0, -1.0, -0.3)).normalized()
    for side in ("l", "r"):
        up, lo, ha = ("%s_%s" % (b, side) for b in ARM_CHAIN)
        palm_local = rest[ha].to_3x3().inverted() @ Vector((0, 0, -1))
        hand_rel = rest[lo].inverted() @ rest[ha]
        raised, turns = [], []
        prev = 0.0
        for i in range(n):
            sh, el, wr = (world[b][i].translation for b in (up, lo, ha))
            axis = (wr - el).normalized()
            palm = world[ha][i].to_3x3() @ palm_local
            p = palm - axis * palm.dot(axis)
            t = forward - axis * forward.dot(axis)
            r = smooth01(0.15, 0.55, (wr - sh).normalized().z) * smooth01(0.25, 0.55, t.length)
            a = prev
            if r > 0.0 and p.length > 1e-4:
                a = math.atan2(axis.dot(p.cross(t)), p.dot(t))
                while a - prev > math.pi:
                    a -= 2 * math.pi
                while a - prev < -math.pi:
                    a += 2 * math.pi
            elif r == 0.0:
                a = 0.0
            prev = a
            raised.append(r)
            turns.append(r * max(-PALM_TURN, min(PALM_TURN, a)))
        turns = gauss(turns, 2.0, loop)
        raised = gauss(raised, 2.0, loop)
        peak_turn = peak_bend = 0.0
        for i in range(n):
            a, r = turns[i], raised[i]
            if r < 1e-4:
                continue
            peak_turn = max(peak_turn, abs(a))
            sh, wr = world[up][i].translation.copy(), world[ha][i].translation.copy()
            fix = about(sh, (wr - sh).normalized(), 0.5 * a)
            for b in (up, lo, ha):
                world[b][i] = fix @ world[b][i]
            el, wr = world[lo][i].translation.copy(), world[ha][i].translation.copy()
            axis = (wr - el).normalized()
            world[lo][i] = about(el, axis, 0.3 * a) @ world[lo][i]
            world[ha][i] = about(wr, axis, 0.2 * a) @ about(el, axis, 0.3 * a) @ world[ha][i]
            # Wrist: split the hand's rotation into a twist about the bone and the bend that is left; cut the bend.
            loc, q, _ = (hand_rel.inverted() @ world[lo][i].inverted() @ world[ha][i]).decompose()
            twist = Quaternion((q.w, 0.0, q.y, 0.0))
            if twist.magnitude > 1e-8:
                twist.normalize()
                swing = q @ twist.inverted()
                if swing.w < 0:
                    swing.negate()
                bend = swing.angle
                peak_bend = max(peak_bend, bend)
                if bend > WRIST_BEND:
                    swing = Quaternion(swing.axis, bend - r * (bend - WRIST_BEND))
                    basis = Matrix.Translation(loc) @ (swing @ twist).to_matrix().to_4x4()
                    world[ha][i] = world[lo][i] @ hand_rel @ basis
        log("    hand_%s: raised in %d frames, palm turned up to %.0f deg, wrist bend was up to %.0f deg" % (
            side, sum(1 for r in raised if r > 0.5), math.degrees(peak_turn), math.degrees(peak_bend)))


def add_tie(world, rest, n, loop):
    """The tie hangs from its knot: it lies on the belly, swings sideways with gravity and lags behind the body."""
    knot, mid = rest["tie_01"].translation.copy(), rest["tie_02"].translation.copy()
    tip = Vector(TIE_TIP)
    length = (tip - knot).length
    along = (tip - knot).normalized()
    side = Vector((1, 0, 0))
    out = Vector((0, along.z, -along.y))

    def angles(v):
        return math.atan2(v.dot(side), max(1e-3, v.dot(along))), math.atan2(v.dot(out), max(1e-3, v.dot(along)))

    def direction(phi, theta):
        return (along + side * math.tan(phi) + out * math.tan(theta)).normalized()

    mid_rest = angles(mid - knot)[1]
    chest, floor, targets = [], [], []
    for i in range(n):
        d = world["spine_03"][i] @ rest["spine_03"].inverted()
        inv = d.inverted()
        belly = world["belly"][i] @ rest["belly"].inverted()
        waist = world["spine_01"][i] @ rest["spine_01"].inverted()
        ribs = world["spine_02"][i] @ rest["spine_02"].inverted()
        # Where the body under the tie is now: the tie may lift off it, never sink into it.
        under_tip = inv @ ((belly @ tip) * 0.75 + (waist @ tip) * 0.25) - knot
        under_mid = inv @ ((belly @ mid) * 0.3 + (ribs @ mid) * 0.7) - knot
        low = max(angles(under_tip)[1], angles(under_mid)[1] - mid_rest)
        down = d.to_3x3().inverted() @ Vector((0, 0, -1))
        phi, theta = angles(down)
        phi = max(-0.5, min(0.5, 0.8 * phi))
        theta = min(math.radians(60), max(low, theta))
        chest.append(d)
        floor.append(low)
        targets.append(d @ (knot + direction(phi, theta) * length))
    upper = spring(targets, 2 * math.pi * 2.4, 0.6, loop)
    lower = spring(targets, 2 * math.pi * 1.6, 0.45, loop)
    world["tie_01"], world["tie_02"] = [], []
    peak_side = peak_lift = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        dirs = []
        for sim in (upper, lower):
            phi, theta = angles(chest[i].inverted() @ sim[i] - knot)
            phi = max(-0.55, min(0.55, phi))
            theta = min(math.radians(60), max(floor[i], theta))
            dirs.append(direction(phi, theta))
            peak_side = max(peak_side, abs(phi))
            peak_lift = max(peak_lift, theta - floor[i])
        first = along.rotation_difference(dirs[0])
        second = dirs[0].rotation_difference(dirs[1])
        if second.angle > TIE_BEND:
            second = Quaternion(second.axis, TIE_BEND)
        hang = chest[i] @ Matrix.Translation(knot) @ first.to_matrix().to_4x4() @ Matrix.Translation(-knot)
        bend = Matrix.Translation(mid) @ second.to_matrix().to_4x4() @ Matrix.Translation(-mid)
        world["tie_01"].append(hang @ rest["tie_01"])
        world["tie_02"].append(hang @ bend @ rest["tie_02"])
    return math.degrees(peak_side), math.degrees(peak_lift)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# KIND: offline tool. Rebuilds the Publisher rig and its clips from the Meshy files, then reports the skin tears of
# one pose.
#   bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/rebuild.sh <work_dir> [clip=Idle] [frame=1]
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)"
BLENDER="${BLENDER:-/f/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe}"
OUT="$1"; CLIP="${2:-Idle}"; FRAME="${3:-1}"
FIXED="$ROOT/Art/Models/boss_fixed"
mkdir -p "$OUT"
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/build_rig.py" > "$OUT/build.log" 2>&1
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/rework_clips.py" -- "$FIXED/publisher_rig.blend" "$FIXED/publisher_clips.blend" "$FIXED/clips.json" "$OUT/rework.txt" > "$OUT/rework.log" 2>&1
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/find_tears.py" -- "$FIXED/publisher_clips.blend" "$OUT/tears.txt" "$CLIP" "$FRAME" > "$OUT/tears.log" 2>&1
grep "\[build\]" "$OUT/build.log" || true
head -12 "$OUT/tears.txt"

import sys

import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

args = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:]
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=args[0])
scene = bpy.context.scene
arm = next(o for o in scene.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
action = bpy.data.actions["Charged_Ground_Slam"]
arm.animation_data.action = action
arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
lines = []
for frame in range(1, 92, 3):
    scene.frame_set(frame)
    row = "%3d" % frame
    for s in "lr":
        hand, fore, up = (arm.pose.bones[n + s] for n in ("hand_", "lowerarm_", "upperarm_"))
        palm = hand.matrix.to_3x3() @ (arm.data.bones["hand_" + s].matrix_local.to_3x3().inverted() @ Vector((0, 0, -1)))
        axis = (hand.head - fore.head).normalized()
        d = (hand.head - up.head).normalized()
        fingers = hand.matrix.to_3x3() @ Vector((0, 1, 0))
        row += " | %s arm %5.2f %5.2f %5.2f palm %5.2f %5.2f %5.2f fingers %5.2f %5.2f %5.2f" % (s, *d, *palm, *fingers)
    lines.append(row)
open(args[1], "w").write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# KIND: offline tool. Renders the review material of the Publisher rig: per clip a before/after animation and an
# after key-frame sheet.
#   bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/review_assets.sh <work_dir>
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)"
BLENDER="${BLENDER:-/f/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe}"
OUT="$1"
CLIPS="Idle,Slow_Orc_Walk,Heavy_Hammer_Swing,Kung_Fu_Punch,Charged_Ground_Slam,Hit_Reaction,Knock_Down"
BEFORE="$ROOT/Art/Models/boss_clips/result.animation_fbx_url.fbx"
AFTER="$ROOT/Art/Models/boss_fixed/publisher_clips.blend"
mkdir -p "$OUT/anim"
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/render_poses.py" -- "$BEFORE" "$OUT/before_seq" --clips "$CLIPS" --step 2 --views q3 --size 320 > "$OUT/before_seq.log" 2>&1
"$BLENDER" -b --factory-startup --python "$HERE/render_poses.py" -- "$AFTER" "$OUT/after_seq" --clips "$CLIPS" --step 2 --views q3 --size 320 > "$OUT/after_seq.log" 2>&1
IFS=',' read -ra LIST <<< "$CLIPS"
for c in "${LIST[@]}"; do
  python "$HERE/sheet.py" "$OUT/anim/$c.webp" --fps 15 --pair "$OUT/before_seq" "$OUT/after_seq" "${c}_q3_"
done
bash "$HERE/preview.sh" "$OUT/after" "$CLIPS" 6 q3,q3b "$AFTER" 320
echo "review assets done"

Sat 14 Nov 2026. The Meshy model of the Publisher on a rebuilt skeleton with new skin weights and the seven Meshy
clips reworked, approved by the author on the art page (Models tab, "Publisher rig":
https://claude.ai/artifact/JPCnbPCnQkjLDX57abegRW) and exported for Unreal. **Nothing is imported into the project
yet and nothing here was checked in Unreal** (the Unreal MCP did not connect in the rig session). Everything below
was checked in Blender 5.2 unless it says otherwise.

## Summary

- **Use `SK_Publisher.fbx` plus the eight clip files of this folder.** Do not mix them with `Art/Models/boss_rig` or
  `boss_clips`: the bone names match, the joint positions do not.
- **What was wrong with the Meshy rig:** the shoulder joint sat about 25 cm inside the chest and the elbow at the
  armpit, the jacket front hung on the clavicles and the head, the upper spine and the neck had almost no weight, the
  thighs reached into the belly. Every arm or head move tore the jacket.
- **What is fixed:** joints moved to where the body bends, weights painted from scratch (belly, chest and jacket on
  the pelvis and the three spine bones, 4 influences at most, normalised), a `root` bone and four helper bones added
  (belly follow-through, three jacket flaps), every clip put on the origin and on the ground, arms kept out of the
  torso, travel moved to `root`.
- **Open risk:** the Unreal import is untested. The first thing to look at after import is the scale (260 cm tall)
  and the facing (see "Import").

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `SK_Publisher.fbx` | Mesh (12 784 verts, one material), skeleton (27 bones), four 2048 px textures embedded (base colour, normal, metallic, roughness). No animation. |
| `Idle.fbx`, `Slow_Orc_Walk.fbx`, `Heavy_Hammer_Swing.fbx`, `Kung_Fu_Punch.fbx`, `Charged_Ground_Slam.fbx`, `Hit_Reaction.fbx`, `Knock_Down.fbx` | One clip each, skeleton only, 30 fps, a key on every frame. Same names as in `boss_clips`. |
| `T_Pose.fbx` | Two frames of the rest pose (arms out). |
| `clips.json` | Frames, seconds, loop flag and root travel of every clip, for code or import scripts. |
| `export_check.txt` | The read-back check of the FBX files (bones, ranges, positions). |
| `publisher_rig.blend`, `publisher_clips.blend` | Sources: the rig with the original Meshy motion, and the reworked clips the FBX files are exported from. |

Rebuild from the Meshy files: `bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/rebuild.sh <work_dir>`, then
`bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export.sh <work_dir>` (Blender 5.2, headless).

## Skeleton

27 bones: the 22 Meshy names, `root`, and four helpers. The FBX data is in centimetres with unit scale 1 and no
scaled armature node; the top node is called `Armature` (Unreal drops a node of that name), so `root` should arrive
as the root bone.

```
root
  pelvis
    spine_01
      spine_02
        spine_03
          neck_01 > head
          clavicle_l > upperarm_l > lowerarm_l > hand_l
          clavicle_r > upperarm_r > lowerarm_r > hand_r
      belly                (helper)
      jacket_front_l       (helper)
      jacket_front_r       (helper)
    thigh_l > calf_l > foot_l > ball_l
    thigh_r > calf_r > foot_r > ball_r
    jacket_back            (helper)
```

- `root` sits on the ground at the origin and carries no skin. It moves only in the three travel clips.
- `belly` is keyed in every clip: a damped follow-through of the belly, 5 cm at most.
- `jacket_front_l`, `jacket_front_r`, `jacket_back` are keyed in every clip: the jacket skirt hangs, lags and yields
  to the thighs. They are plain animated bones: no physics asset or cloth is needed for them. If the game blends
  clips, they blend like any other bone.
- No fingers, no face bones (Meshy made none). No sockets: a weapon or effect attaches to `hand_l` / `hand_r`.

## Clips

30 fps. Frame counts and travel come from `clips.json`. X and Y are Blender axes: he faces -Y, +X is his left.

| Clip | Frames | Seconds | Loop | Root travel | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idle` | 121 | 4.0 | yes | none | Look-around idle. A side-on stance: the hips are turned 45 to 60 degrees to his right while the head looks forward. |
| `Slow_Orc_Walk` | 166 | 5.5 | yes | none, in place | Heavy hunched walk. The feet do not slide at about 0.43 m/s (43 cm/s) at import scale. |
| `Heavy_Hammer_Swing` | 56 | 1.83 | no | none | Two-hand overhead blow. Same side-on stance. |
| `Charged_Ground_Slam` | 91 | 3.0 | no | none | Wind-up and a blow into the ground. |
| `Hit_Reaction` | 50 | 1.63 | no | 104 cm to his left | A stagger. Travel on `root`. |
| `Knock_Down` | 76 | 2.5 | no | 78 cm back | Thrown onto his back; the death clip. Travel on `root`. Hold the last frame. |
| `Kung_Fu_Punch` | 220 | 7.3 | no | 150 cm to his right, 69 cm back | A long form with spins, kicks and a roll; ends facing backwards. Kept whole on the author's word; too long and too acrobatic for a plain attack, so use it only as a special, or leave it out. |

- **Loops:** `Idle` and `Slow_Orc_Walk` are the Meshy loops unchanged in timing; the first and the last frame are
  the same pose (measured: every bone within 0.1 cm in `Idle`; in the walk all within 0.8 cm, the largest being the
  belly helper).
- **Travel:** in the three travel clips the horizontal travel of the body is on `root` (smoothed), the rest of the
  motion on `pelvis`. Play them with root motion on to move the actor, or with root motion off and Force Root Lock on
  to keep him in place. The other clips have a still `root`.
- **Ground:** every clip stands on Z = 0 and starts at the origin (the walk is centred on it).
- **Scale of the times and distances:** all of the above is at import scale, where he is 260 cm tall. If the actor
  is scaled, travel and walk speed scale with it.

## Import (not verified in Unreal)

1. Import `SK_Publisher.fbx` as a skeletal mesh with a new skeleton. Expected: 27 bones with `root` as the root,
   260 cm tall, feet on Z = 0, facing +Y (the usual Unreal character convention: turn the mesh -90 degrees yaw in
   the actor, as for the mannequin). Import normals from the file; the textures are embedded.
2. Import the eight clip files as animations onto that skeleton, 30 fps, no mesh. Each file holds one take; Blender reads it
   back as `Armature|<clip>`, so name the assets after the files if the importer offers the take name.
3. Enable root motion on `Hit_Reaction`, `Knock_Down` and `Kung_Fu_Punch` if the game should use their travel;
   otherwise set Force Root Lock.
4. Set `Idle` and `Slow_Orc_Walk` to loop.
5. If the size is wrong by a factor of 100, the importer converted units that were already centimetres: turn its
   unit conversion off (or set a uniform import scale) instead of scaling the actor, so the root travel stays right.

Checked on the files by reading them back into Blender (`export_check.txt`): 27 bones with one root, 4 influences
at most and all weights normalised, 260 cm tall, every clip has its full frame range, and every bone is within
0.001 cm of the source at the first, middle and last frame of every clip.

## Known limits

- When the head turns far (`Idle`, about 60 degrees), the black shirt collar under the jowls stretches. The skin of
  the head and the collar are one closed Meshy surface there, so something has to give; it reads as a shadow under
  the chin at game distance.
- The mesh is one fused Meshy shell: the tie, the lapels and the jacket edge are not separate cloth, they are skinned
  with the chest under them. They do not flap on their own.
- The motion is the Meshy library motion, cleaned and grounded, not new animation: the timing of the attacks (where
  the hit lands) was not changed. Hit frames by eye in Blender were not measured; take them from the clip in Unreal.
- The source model, rig and clips are Meshy output (see `THIRD_PARTY.md`); this folder is our rework of them.

  armpit, the jacket front hung on the clavicles and the head, the upper spine and the neck had almost no weight, the
  thighs reached into the belly. Every arm or head move tore the jacket.

  import `SK_Publisher.fbx` and all clips again onto a new skeleton.

    spine_01
      spine_02
        spine_03

          clavicle_r > upperarm_r > lowerarm_r > hand_r

# The Publisher: rebuilt rig and clips (hand-over)

Sat 14 Nov 2026. The Meshy model of the Publisher on a rebuilt skeleton with new skin weights and the seven Meshy
clips reworked, approved by the author on the art page (Models tab, "Publisher rig":
https://claude.ai/artifact/JPCnbPCnQkjLDX57abegRW) and exported for Unreal. **Nothing is imported into the project
yet and nothing here was checked in Unreal** (the Unreal MCP did not connect in the rig session). Everything below
was checked in Blender 5.2 unless it says otherwise.

## Summary

- **Use `SK_Publisher.fbx` plus the eight clip files of this folder.** Do not mix them with `Art/Models/boss_rig` or
  `boss_clips`: the bone names match, the joint positions do not.
- **What was wrong with the Meshy rig:** the shoulder joint sat about 25 cm inside the chest and the elbow at the
  armpit, the jacket front hung on the clavicles and the head, the upper spine and the neck had almost no weight, the
  thighs reached into the belly. Every arm or head move tore the jacket.
- **What is fixed:** joints moved to where the body bends, weights painted from scratch (belly, chest and jacket on
  the pelvis and the three spine bones, 4 influences at most, normalised), a `root` bone and six helper bones added
  (belly follow-through, three jacket flaps, two tie bones), every clip put on the origin and on the ground, arms
  kept out of the torso, travel moved to `root`.
- **Changed late on Sat 14 Nov (second export):** the skeleton grew from 27 to 29 bones (`tie_01`, `tie_02`), and
  in `Charged_Ground_Slam` the raised hand turns its palm forward. If the first export was already imported,
  import `SK_Publisher.fbx` and all clips again onto a new skeleton.
- **Open risk:** the Unreal import is untested. The first thing to look at after import is the scale (260 cm tall)
  and the facing (see "Import").

## Files

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `SK_Publisher.fbx` | Mesh (12 784 verts, one material), skeleton (29 bones), four 2048 px textures embedded (base colour, normal, metallic, roughness). No animation. |
| `Idle.fbx`, `Slow_Orc_Walk.fbx`, `Heavy_Hammer_Swing.fbx`, `Kung_Fu_Punch.fbx`, `Charged_Ground_Slam.fbx`, `Hit_Reaction.fbx`, `Knock_Down.fbx` | One clip each, skeleton only, 30 fps, a key on every frame. Same names as in `boss_clips`. |
| `T_Pose.fbx` | Two frames of the rest pose (arms out). |
| `clips.json` | Frames, seconds, loop flag and root travel of every clip, for code or import scripts. |
| `export_check.txt` | The read-back check of the FBX files (bones, ranges, positions). |
| `publisher_rig.blend`, `publisher_clips.blend` | Sources: the rig with the original Meshy motion, and the reworked clips the FBX files are exported from. |

Rebuild from the Meshy files: `bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/rebuild.sh <work_dir>`, then
`bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/export.sh <work_dir>` (Blender 5.2, headless).

## Skeleton

29 bones: the 22 Meshy names, `root`, and six helpers. The FBX data is in centimetres with unit scale 1 and no
scaled armature node; the top node is called `Armature` (Unreal drops a node of that name), so `root` should arrive
as the root bone.

```
root
  pelvis
    spine_01
      spine_02
        spine_03
          neck_01 > head
          clavicle_l > upperarm_l > lowerarm_l > hand_l
          clavicle_r > upperarm_r > lowerarm_r > hand_r
          tie_01 > tie_02  (helpers)
      belly                (helper)
      jacket_front_l       (helper)
      jacket_front_r       (helper)
    thigh_l > calf_l > foot_l > ball_l
    thigh_r > calf_r > foot_r > ball_r
    jacket_back            (helper)
```

- `root` sits on the ground at the origin and carries no skin. It moves only in the three travel clips.
- `belly` is keyed in every clip: a damped follow-through of the belly, 5 cm at most.
- `jacket_front_l`, `jacket_front_r`, `jacket_back` are keyed in every clip: the jacket skirt hangs, lags and yields
  to the thighs. They are plain animated bones: no physics asset or cloth is needed for them. If the game blends
  clips, they blend like any other bone.
- `tie_01` (from the knot) and `tie_02` (the lower half) are keyed in every clip: the tie hangs from its knot, lies
  on the belly, follows gravity sideways, lifts off when he bends forward and lags a little. Plain animated bones
  as well.
- No fingers, no face bones (Meshy made none). No sockets: a weapon or effect attaches to `hand_l` / `hand_r`.

## Clips

30 fps. Frame counts and travel come from `clips.json`. X and Y are Blender axes: he faces -Y, +X is his left.

| Clip | Frames | Seconds | Loop | Root travel | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Idle` | 121 | 4.0 | yes | none | Look-around idle. A side-on stance: the hips are turned 45 to 60 degrees to his right while the head looks forward. |
| `Slow_Orc_Walk` | 166 | 5.5 | yes | none, in place | Heavy hunched walk. The feet do not slide at about 0.43 m/s (43 cm/s) at import scale. |
| `Heavy_Hammer_Swing` | 56 | 1.83 | no | none | Two-hand overhead blow. Same side-on stance. |
| `Charged_Ground_Slam` | 91 | 3.0 | no | none | Wind-up and a blow into the ground. The raised hand (right in the wind-up, left after the blow) is turned palm forward and kept in line with the forearm. |
| `Hit_Reaction` | 50 | 1.63 | no | 104 cm to his left | A stagger. Travel on `root`. |
| `Knock_Down` | 76 | 2.5 | no | 78 cm back | Thrown onto his back; the death clip. Travel on `root`. Hold the last frame. |
| `Kung_Fu_Punch` | 220 | 7.3 | no | 150 cm to his right, 69 cm back | A long form with spins, kicks and a roll; ends facing backwards. Kept whole on the author's word; too long and too acrobatic for a plain attack, so use it only as a special, or leave it out. |
| `T_Pose` | 2 | 0.03 | yes | none | Rest pose, for retargeting or as a reference pose. |

- **Loops:** `Idle` and `Slow_Orc_Walk` are the Meshy loops unchanged in timing; the first and the last frame are
  the same pose (measured: every bone within 0.1 cm in `Idle`; in the walk all within 0.8 cm, the largest being the
  belly helper).
- **Travel:** in the three travel clips the horizontal travel of the body is on `root` (smoothed), the rest of the
  motion on `pelvis`. Play them with root motion on to move the actor, or with root motion off and Force Root Lock on
  to keep him in place. The other clips have a still `root`.
- **Ground:** every clip stands on Z = 0 and starts at the origin (the walk is centred on it).
- **Scale of the times and distances:** all of the above is at import scale, where he is 260 cm tall. If the actor
  is scaled, travel and walk speed scale with it.

## Import (not verified in Unreal)

1. Import `SK_Publisher.fbx` as a skeletal mesh with a new skeleton. Expected: 29 bones with `root` as the root,
   260 cm tall, feet on Z = 0, facing +Y (the usual Unreal character convention: turn the mesh -90 degrees yaw in
   the actor, as for the mannequin). Import normals from the file; the textures are embedded.
2. Import the eight clip files as animations onto that skeleton, 30 fps, no mesh. Each file holds one take; Blender reads it
   back as `Armature|<clip>`, so name the assets after the files if the importer offers the take name.
3. Enable root motion on `Hit_Reaction`, `Knock_Down` and `Kung_Fu_Punch` if the game should use their travel;
   otherwise set Force Root Lock.
4. Set `Idle` and `Slow_Orc_Walk` to loop.
5. If the size is wrong by a factor of 100, the importer converted units that were already centimetres: turn its
   unit conversion off (or set a uniform import scale) instead of scaling the actor, so the root travel stays right.

Checked on the files by reading them back into Blender (`export_check.txt`): 29 bones with one root, 4 influences
at most and all weights normalised, 260 cm tall, every clip has its full frame range, and every bone is within
0.001 cm of the source at the first, middle and last frame of every clip.

## Known limits

- When the head turns far (`Idle`, about 60 degrees), the black shirt collar under the jowls stretches. The skin of
  the head and the collar are one closed Meshy surface there, so something has to give; it reads as a shadow under
  the chin at game distance.
- The mesh is one fused Meshy shell: the tie, the lapels and the jacket edge are not separate cloth, they are skinned
  with the chest under them. They do not flap on their own.
- The motion is the Meshy library motion, cleaned and grounded, not new animation: the timing of the attacks (where
  the hit lands) was not changed. Hit frames by eye in Blender were not measured; take them from the clip in Unreal.
- The source model, rig and clips are Meshy output (see `THIRD_PARTY.md`); this folder is our rework of them.

    p = probe[clip]
    a, b = p["frames"][str(p["first"])], p["frames"][str(p["last"])]
    worst = max((math.dist(a[k], b[k]), k) for k in a)
    print(clip, "first vs last, worst bone gap cm: %.2f %s" % worst)

file.content:
- What works: the Meshy auto-rig tore the jacket on every arm and head move (shoulder joint 25 cm inside the chest,
  jacket front weighted to the clavicles and the head). Rebuilt in headless Blender 5.2 by our scripts
  (`Tools/Art/publisher_rig`): joints refitted under the same bone names, weights painted from scratch from rest
  position and texture colour (4 influences, normalised), a `root` bone, a belly helper with a damped follow-through
  and three jacket flap bones. The seven clips reworked: on the origin and on the ground, arms kept out of the torso,
  travel on `root`, plus a T-pose. Before and after on the art page (Models tab), approved by the author, exported as
  `SK_Publisher.fbx` and one FBX per clip to `Art/Models/boss_fixed` with `README.md` as the import notes. Read back
  into Blender: 27 bones, every bone within 0.001 cm of the source. Tool: Claude Code.
- What went wrong: the author found a lapel sticking out in the idle: shaded creases of the collar passed the skin
  colour test and were painted as head; the head set is now only what joins the skull, and stacked layers (lapel,
  jacket edge, tie) share weights over space. The first FBX export scaled the mesh twice (260 m tall), caught by the
  read-back check. Not imported into Unreal and not checked there: the Unreal MCP did not connect in this session.

Both fixes are in, exported and committed (`b77b290`, not pushed); the artifact is at version 10: https://claude.ai/artifact/JPCnbPCnQkjLDX57abegRW (Models tab, "Publisher rig").

Next for you: play Idle and Charged Ground Slam in the viewer and tell me whether the tie swing is the right amount. Its sideways swing reaches 22° in Idle and 32° in the attacks, which may be more than "slightly"; it is one constant to turn down.

@RTK.md

# Рабочий флоу по умолчанию

Структурированный флоу — это: обсуждение → грил (/grilling) → тикеты → реализация через TDD (/tdd, красный-зелёный на согласованных швах).

Перед стартом каждой НОВОЙ задачи (не подзадачи текущей) реши, нужен ли он:

- **Уверен, что флоу не нужен** — скипай молча, не спрашивая, и сразу берись за работу. Это про мелкие правки, однострочники, операционные и разведочные действия, ответы на вопросы, правку конфигов и доков.
- **Уверен, что нужен, или сомневаешься** — спроси одним коротким вопросом, каким именно флоу вести (полный / только обсуждение + грил / без флоу). Задал вопрос — жди ответа, не начинай работу до него.

Для чисто исследовательских и операционных задач без производственного кода (разведка API, генерация контента, публикация) в вопросе сразу отметь, что TDD-часть там применить не к чему — уместны только обсуждение и грил.

# Бюджет лимитов: прогноз перед тяжёлым запуском

Перед любым запуском, который может съесть заметную часть 5-часового лимита, сначала
напиши в чат прогноз и жди моего явного «да». Тяжёлым считается: Workflow (любой),
больше 3 субагентов разом или в цикле, фоновые агенты на длинные задачи. Правило
действует всегда, в том числе в ultracode-сессиях: ultracode разрешает workflow, но не
отменяет прогноз и подтверждение.

В прогнозе:
- сколько агентов (с учётом верификаторов и циклов, худший случай);
- грубая оценка токенов (ориентир: агент-исследователь 50-150k, Opus дороже Sonnet);
- примерная доля 5-часового лимита и время;
- дешёвый вариант (меньше агентов, Sonnet или Haiku, без верификации) рядом с полным.

Хук `workflow-guard` на каждый Workflow запрашивает моё подтверждение, но прогноз
в чате должен прийти до вызова, а не вместо него. Если запуск уже идёт и расход
растёт быстрее прогноза, остановись и скажи.

# Стиль письма

**Длинные тире.** По умолчанию ставь запятую, двоеточие или скобки там, где
напрашивается «—». Тире оставляй для настоящего разрыва мысли, и не чаще одного
раза на длинный текст. Правило касается всего, что пишешь ты: ответы в терминале,
комментарии к PR и ревью, сообщения коммитов, документация, отчёты. Мой
собственный текст не переписывай, если об этом не просили.

**Язык в коде, коммитах и пул-реквестах.** Комментарии в коде, сообщения коммитов
(git и dv), комментарии, ревью и описания PR всегда по-английски, даже если
окружающий код прокомментирован по-русски или коллега в треде пишет по-русски.
Старые русские комментарии не переводи, если об этом не просили. Разговор со мной
в терминале, наоборот, по-русски.


# Shell и деструктивные операции

- **Никаких heredoc и многострочных строк с backslash-экранированием в Bash.** Всё
  многострочное (скрипты, JSON, тексты) пишется в файл через Write, потом файл
  исполняется или читается. Хук `bash-guard` блокирует heredoc автоматически.
- **Деструктивные операции** (rm -rf, drop, truncate, delete from, firestore delete,
  git clean и т.п.) только через скрипт-файл с флагом `--dry-run`, включённым по
  умолчанию. Сначала прогон в dry-run с точными счётчиками, потом остановка и
  ожидание моего явного «да». Хук переводит такие команды в режим подтверждения.
- Перед `git push`: перейти в корень репозитория и показать `pwd`.

# Проверяй, прежде чем утверждать

- Любое утверждение о нашем коде, PR, стороннем API, статусе внешнего сервиса или
  игровой механике сначала проверяется по источнику: файл, документация, ответ API.
  В ответе указывай, что именно проверено и где.
- Если проверить нельзя, пиши «не проверено» явно, а не утверждай.

# Формат ответов

- По умолчанию коротко: сначала ответ, потом детали, если нужны. Не пересказывай
  мне мой же план обратно.
- Первая строка ответа: сам ответ или действие. Без вступлений вроде «Сейчас
  сделаю…», «Отличный вопрос».
- В конце одно конкретное следующее действие (моё или твоё), если что-то
  осталось открытым. Без «обращайся, если что».
- Без пересказа сделанного после задачи: только что теперь работает и что
  проверено.
- Списки до 5 пунктов. Больше: сгруппируй и поставь важное первым, остальное
  отдай по запросу.
- Ответ в чате читается за 10-20 секунд. Большой материал (список тикетов,
  таблица, план на десятки пунктов) не вываливай в чат: пиши в файл, в чат
  дай сводку из 3-5 строк и путь.
- В многошаговой работе пиши, где мы: «шаг 3 из 5: …, дальше …».
- Правила из «Проверяй, прежде чем утверждать» и саммари к текстам остаются
  в силе: краткость их не отменяет.
  (Основано на скилле ayghri/i-have-adhd, принято на постоянку 2026-11-01.)
- Тексты для Slack, Telegram, почты и клиентов: только plain text, без
  markdown-таблиц и заголовков, до 5 строк, если я не просил больше.

# Коммуникации: отправка только по моему прямому указанию

- В Slack, почту, мессенджеры и подобные каналы ты отправляешь только тогда,
  когда я прямо попросил отправить именно это сообщение в текущем разговоре.
  По собственной инициативе никогда: по умолчанию ты готовишь текст, вставляю
  и отправляю я. Хук `comms-guard` на каждую отправку (сообщение, файл в канал,
  письмо) запрашивает моё подтверждение. Комментарии и ревью в PR это не
  касается.
- К каждому подготовленному тексту прилагай короткое саммари на русском
  (1-3 строки): кому, о чём, что важно. Сам текст на языке адресата.

# Дисциплина скоупа

- Ревью, аудит, написание тикетов: на выходе только находки и тикеты. Правки
  только после явного «implement» / «сделай».
- Не добавляй в план пункты, которых я не просил. Помечай их как необязательные
  предложения отдельным списком.

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# MegaJam 2026: project rules

Everything is in **English**: the conversation with the author, code, comments, commits, the dev log and every text
in the game (jam rule: the submission must be playable and judged in English; the session logs are part of the dev
log). The author may write in Russian; reply in English anyway.

## Hard rules

1. **Jam window: 2026-11-12 05:00 UTC to 2026-11-16 01:59 UTC.** Everything in the game (gameplay code, levels,
   art, sound) is made inside it. Before the start only tooling exists: see `PREJAM.md`. Rules and deadlines are in
   `JAM_BRIEF.md`.
2. **Engine: UE 5.8**, module `JamGame`, tests `Jam.<Area>.<Case>`, log category `LogJamGame`.
3. **Build and tests: `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh`.** The script closes only this project's editor, the full
   build needs no permission. New `check_code.py` warnings are fixed or justified in one line.
4. **The MCP server of this project is on port 8002** (Diskworld 8000, CastleFight 8001).
5. **Version control: git + LFS.** Commit after Save All in the editor, otherwise an old `.uasset` gets in. Never
   amend: each commit is evidence of when the work was done.
6. **Agent logs are part of the submission evidence.** `Tools/Git/hooks/pre-commit` exports every Claude Code
   session of this project to `_AgentLogs/` on each commit. Enable once per clone:
   `git config core.hooksPath Tools/Git/hooks`. A session run from another folder is listed in
   `Tools/Devlog/sessions.json`.
7. **Third-party content is declared.** Every asset, plugin, model or sound that the team did not make during the
   jam goes to `THIRD_PARTY.md` with its source and licence at the moment it is added.
8. **Deleting files** only through a script with a dry run by default and the author's explicit yes.

## Working cycle

- Production code is written test-first: a `Jam.` test before the code, decisions in pure `*Rules`
  (`.claude/rules/cpp.md`).
- Packaging: `bash Tools/Build/package.sh --config Shipping --name TeamName_GameName`, then
  `bash Tools/Build/smoke_package.sh`. Warn the author before a smoke run: it opens a game window.
- The dev log is `DEVLOG.md`: a few lines per working block (what was done, which AI tool, what went wrong).
- [Aim feel reference](aim-feel-reference.md) — Hades 2: instant turn to the mouse, visible cursor, no crosshair

### 22:05 The Publisher's rig, round 3: a tie of its own and the slam hand

- What works: two findings of the author fixed in `Tools/Art/publisher_rig`. The tie was skinned to the chest and the
  belly, so it bent when the torso twisted in the idle: it now has two bones (`tie_01`, `tie_02`, 29 bones in all)
  and a baked motion: it hangs from the knot, lies on the belly, follows gravity sideways, lifts off when he bends
  forward and lags a little. In `Charged_Ground_Slam` the raised hand was cocked back with the palm up: the raised
  arm now turns its palm forward (the turn shared by arm, forearm and hand) and the wrist bend is cut to 12 degrees.
  All FBX files exported again and read back (29 bones, every bone within 0.001 cm), art page and `README.md`
  updated. Tool: Claude Code.
- What went wrong: the skeleton changed after the first export, so anything imported from it has to be imported
  again. Still not checked in Unreal: the Unreal MCP did not connect.

file.content:
- What works: the Meshy auto-rig tore the jacket on every arm and head move (shoulder joint 25 cm inside the chest,
  jacket front weighted to the clavicles and the head). Rebuilt in headless Blender 5.2 by our scripts
  (`Tools/Art/publisher_rig`): joints refitted under the same bone names, weights painted from scratch from rest
  position and texture colour (4 influences, normalised), a `root` bone, a belly helper with a damped follow-through
  and three jacket flap bones. The seven clips reworked: on the origin and on the ground, arms kept out of the torso,
  travel on `root`, plus a T-pose. Before and after on the art page (Models tab), approved by the author, exported as
  `SK_Publisher.fbx` and one FBX per clip to `Art/Models/boss_fixed` with `README.md` as the import notes. Read back
  into Blender: 27 bones, every bone within 0.001 cm of the source. Tool: Claude Code.
- What went wrong: the author found a lapel sticking out in the idle: shaded creases of the collar passed the skin
  colour test and were painted as head; the head set is now only what joins the skull, and stacked layers (lapel,
  jacket edge, tie) share weights over space. The first FBX export scaled the mesh twice (260 m tall), caught by the
  read-back check. Not imported into Unreal and not checked there: the Unreal MCP did not connect in this session.
