346	    # Head and neck: the skin is the head; the twist is spread over the jowls and a short ring of the collar.
347	    out = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(head)[0], 0.4)
348	    inside = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(~head)[0], 0.4)
349	    # The skin border lies in the crease under the jowls and its texture is ragged: the first ring of black collar
350	    # moves with the skin, so the stretch falls on plain black shirt further out.
351	    reach = np.where(black, np.maximum(out - NECK_RING, 0.0), out)
352	    hn = np.where(head, 1.0, 1 - ss(0.0, 0.12, reach))
353	    w_head = np.where(head, 0.6 + 0.4 * ss(0.0, 0.10, inside), 0.6 * (1 - ss(0.0, 0.07, reach)))
354	    for k in names:
355	        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hn)
356	    w["head"] = w_head
357	    w["neck_01"] = np.maximum(hn - w_head, 0.0)
358	
359	    # Tie: the gold strip on the shirt hangs from the knot on its own two bones.
360	    gold = (hsv[:, 0] > 0.07) & (hsv[:, 0] < 0.17) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.45) & (hsv[:, 2] > 0.3)
361	    tie = gold & ~head & (ax < 0.12) & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16)
362	    # Dark texels inside the gold would leave holes in the strip: whatever lies inside its outline is tie as well.
363	    rows = np.clip(((z - 1.45) / 0.02).astype(int), 0, 35)
364	    half = np.zeros(36)
365	    np.maximum.at(half, rows[tie], ax[tie])
366	    half = np.maximum(half, np.maximum(np.roll(half, 1), np.roll(half, -1)))
367	    tie = tie | (~head & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16) & (ax < half[rows] - 0.005))
368	    # Notches in the outline go the same way: a vert with most of its neighbours in the tie is tie.
369	    for _ in range(2):
370	        share = np.array([tie[nb].mean() if len(nb) else 0.0 for nb in adj])
371	        tie = tie | (~head & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16) & (share > 0.5))
372	    # The knot itself stays on the chest; the faces that join it to the strip must stay gold.
373	    knot = gold & ~tie & ~head & (ax < 0.12) & (y < -0.15) & (z > 2.0)
374	    hang = np.where(tie, ss(2.12, 2.00, z), 0.0)
375	    lower = ss(1.88, 1.72, z)
376	    for k in names:
377	        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hang)
378	    w["tie_01"] = hang * (1 - lower)
379	    w["tie_02"] = hang * lower
380	    # The knot sits on the chest: it must not follow the head.
381	    for k in ("head", "neck_01"):
382	        w["spine_03"] = w["spine_03"] + np.where(tie, w[k], 0.0)
383	        w[k] = np.where(tie, 0.0, w[k])
384	    print("[build] tie verts %d" % tie.sum())

386	    W = np.stack([w[k] for k in names], axis=1)
387	    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

389	    # Smooth over the surface, then put the rigid parts back.
390	    rigid = (head & (inside > 0.08)) | (ax > WRIST_X + 0.08) | (z < 0.12) | tie
391	    fixed = W.copy()
392	    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
393	    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
394	    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
395	    for _ in range(6):
396	        avg = np.zeros_like(W)
397	        np.add.at(avg, idx, W[nbr])
398	        avg /= deg[:, None]
399	        W = 0.5 * W + 0.5 * avg
400	        W[rigid] = fixed[rigid]

402	    # Layers that lie on each other (lapel on jacket, jacket edge on shirt, tie on shirt) are not neighbours on the
403	    # surface, so the smoothing drives them apart: average the torso over space as well.

418	    W = np.where(keep & (W > 0.01), W, 0.0)

432	    split_tie(mesh, co, W, names, tie, knot, black & ~tie & ~head)

435	def clean_neck_texture(mesh, adj, rgb, head, shirt, inside, out):
436	    """Make the skin-to-collar border of the base colour follow the mesh.
437	
438	    Meshy paints that border across the faces, ragged, with black spilled onto the jowls and skin onto the collar; it
439	    shows as soon as the head turns. Near the border the faces are repainted: skin on one side of a smooth line
440	    over the mesh, black on the other.
441	    """
442	    me = mesh.data
443	    image = base_image(me)
444	    w, h = image.size
445	    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
446	    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
447	    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
448	    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2) * (w, h) - 0.5
449	    near_skin = head & (inside < 0.10) & (rgb.max(axis=1) > 0.4)
450	    tone = np.median(rgb[near_skin], axis=0)
451	    black_px = np.array((0.015, 0.015, 0.015))
452	
453	    def is_skin(c):
454	        hi, lo = c.max(axis=-1), c.min(axis=-1)
455	        return (hi > 0.5) & ((hi - lo) > 0.2 * hi) & (c[..., 0] >= c[..., 1])
456	
457	    # The border: where the skin flag, smoothed over the surface, crosses one half. Lone skin spikes in the crease
458	    # fall on the black side.
459	    side = head.astype(float)
460	    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
461	    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
462	    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
463	    for _ in range(4):
464	        avg = np.zeros(len(side))
465	        np.add.at(avg, idx, side[nbr])
466	        side = 0.5 * side + 0.5 * avg / deg
467	    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
468	    me.calc_loop_triangles()
469	    done = texels = 0
470	    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
471	        v = np.array(lt.vertices)
472	        hv = head[v]
473	        if not (band[v].any() and (hv | shirt[v]).all()):
474	            continue
475	        p = uv[np.array(lt.loops)]
476	        x0, y0 = np.floor(p.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
477	        x1, y1 = np.ceil(p.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
478	        x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
479	        if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0:
480	            continue
481	        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
482	        d = (p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (p[0, 1] - p[2, 1])
483	        if abs(d) < 1e-9:
484	            continue
485	        b0 = ((p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
486	        b1 = ((p[2, 1] - p[0, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
487	        b2 = 1 - b0 - b1
488	        tol = min(0.5, 1.5 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
489	        cover = (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (b2 >= -tol)
490	        block = px[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1, :3]
491	        share = b0 * side[v[0]] + b1 * side[v[1]] + b2 * side[v[2]]
492	        to_skin = cover & (share > 0.5) & ~is_skin(block)
493	        to_black = cover & (share <= 0.5)
494	        own = block[cover & is_skin(block)]
495	        block[to_skin] = np.median(own, axis=0) if len(own) >= 4 else tone
496	        block[to_black] = black_px
497	        done += 1
498	        texels += int(to_skin.sum() + to_black.sum())
499	    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
500	    image.update()
501	    image.pack()
502	    print("[build] neck texture: %d faces, %d texels repainted, tone %s" % (done, texels, tone.round(3)))

505	def split_tie(mesh, co, W, names, tie, knot, shirt):
506	    """Cut the tie loose from the shirt it is modelled into.
507	
508	    The tie faces are copied as a free two-sided strip that keeps the tie weights; the faces they came from stay on
509	    the body as plain black shirt, so nothing stretches between the two when the tie swings away. The faces that
510	    join the knot to the strip turn plain gold and stay where they are: black or sunk, they show as a wedge under
511	    the knot.
512	    """
513	    me = mesh.data
514	    bm = bmesh.new()
515	    bm.from_mesh(me)
516	    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
517	    bm.normal_update()
518	    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
519	    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
520	    join = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and any(knot[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
521	    held = {v for f in join for v in f.verts}
522	    touching = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and f not in join]
523	    donor = next(f for f in bm.faces if all(shirt[v.index] and abs(v.co.x) > 0.15 and v.co.y < -0.2
524	                                             and 1.6 < v.co.z < 1.9 for v in f.verts))
525	    black_uv = sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)
526	    donor = min(faces, key=lambda f: (f.calc_center_median() - Vector(TIE_MID)).length)
527	    gold_uv = sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)
528	
529	    def outward(v):
530	        """Off the chest, never sideways: the folds of the knot have walls that would slide across the strip."""
531	        d = Vector((0.0, min(v.normal.y, -0.3), v.normal.z))
532	        return d.normalized()
533	
534	    front = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
535	    back = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
536	    for geom, lift in ((front, TIE_LIFT), (back, 0.5 * TIE_LIFT)):
537	        for v in geom:
538	            if isinstance(v, bmesh.types.BMVert):
539	                v.co += outward(v) * lift
540	    bmesh.ops.reverse_faces(bm, faces=[f for f in back if isinstance(f, bmesh.types.BMFace)])
541	    # The shirt under the strip sinks, so a breathing belly does not come through the tie.
542	    for v in {v for f in faces for v in f.verts} - held:
543	        v.co -= outward(v) * TIE_SINK
544	    # Right under the knot the strip hardly leaves the chest, and a crack between its folds must not show black.
545	    under = [f for f in faces if min(v.co.z for v in f.verts) > TIE_GOLD_UNDER]
546	    touching = [f for f in touching if f not in under]
547	    for group, spot in ((touching, black_uv), (join + under, gold_uv)):
548	        for f in group:
549	            for l in f.loops:
550	                l[uv].uv = spot
551	    bm.to_mesh(me)
552	    bm.free()
553	
554	    # The verts left behind move like the shirt around them.
555	    body = np.where(shirt)[0]
556	    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(body))
557	    for k, i in enumerate(body):
558	        tree.insert(co[i], k)
559	    tree.balance()
560	    groups = [mesh.vertex_groups[name] for name in names]
561	    for i in np.where(tie)[0]:
562	        near = [body[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_n(co[i], 6)]
563	        row = W[near].mean(axis=0)
564	        row = np.where(row >= np.sort(row)[-4], row, 0.0)
565	        row /= row.sum()
566	        for g, value in zip(groups, row):
567	            if value > 0:
568	                g.add([int(i)], float(value), "REPLACE")
569	            else:
570	                g.remove([int(i)])
571	    print("[build] tie split: %d faces copied twice, %d turned black, %d gold under the knot, %d verts in all" % (
572	        len(faces), len(touching), len(join), len(me.vertices)))

def paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy):
    me = mesh.data
    n = len(me.vertices)
    co = np.zeros(n * 3)
    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
    x, y, z = co[:, 0], co[:, 1], co[:, 2]
    ax = np.abs(x)
    adj = neighbours(me)
    rgb = vertex_colours(mesh)
    head, black, cream, hsv = head_set(co, rgb, adj)
    red = ((hsv[:, 0] < 0.03) | (hsv[:, 0] > 0.95)) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.6)
    print("[build] head verts %d, black %d, cream %d" % (head.sum(), black.sum(), cream.sum()))

    names = [b.name for b in arm.data.bones]
    w = {name: np.zeros(n) for name in names}

    # Trunk: a partition by height.
    h = 0.14
    s1, s2, s3 = (ss(c - h, c + h, z) for c in SPINE_Z)
    w["pelvis"] = 1 - s1
    w["spine_01"] = s1 * (1 - s2)
    w["spine_02"] = s2 * (1 - s3)
    w["spine_03"] = s3
    trunk = ["pelvis", "spine_01", "spine_02", "spine_03"]

    def scale(keys, factor):
        for k in keys:
            w[k] = w[k] * factor

    # Belly: the front bulge, shirt and jacket front alike.
    belly = 0.75 * ss(0.08, -0.30, y) * ss(1.95, 1.58, z) * ss(0.98, 1.14, z) * ss(0.72, 0.42, ax)
    scale(trunk, 1 - belly)
    w["belly"] = belly

    # Jacket flaps: the cream skirt of the jacket from the hem up to the waist.
    jacket = (~black & ~red & (z > 1.15)).astype(float)
    flap = 0.85 * ss(1.50, 1.24, z) * jacket
    theta = np.abs(np.arctan2(x, -y))
    back = ss(math.radians(80), math.radians(120), theta)
    scale(trunk + ["belly"], 1 - flap)
    w["jacket_back"] = flap * back
    w["jacket_front_l"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x > 0)
    w["jacket_front_r"] = flap * (1 - back) * (x <= 0)
    body = trunk + ["belly", "jacket_back", "jacket_front_l", "jacket_front_r"]

    # Legs: below a hip line that runs from the crotch up to the outside of the hip, never into the jacket.
    zc = 0.90 + 0.17 * ss(0.0, 0.35, ax)
    leg = ss(zc + 0.13, zc - 0.13, z)
    leg = np.where(black & (z > 0.9), 0.0, leg)
    leg = np.where(z > 1.165, 0.0, leg)
    scale(body, 1 - leg)
    left = ss(-0.05, 0.05, x)
    knee = ss(KNEE_Z + 0.10, KNEE_Z - 0.10, z)
    foot = ss(0.27, 0.15, z)
    for side, share, sx in (("l", left, 1.0), ("r", 1 - left, -1.0)):
        t = (x * sx - ball_xy[0]) * toe_dir[0] + (y - ball_xy[1]) * toe_dir[1]
        toe = ss(-0.04, 0.04, t) * ss(0.16, 0.10, z)
        w["thigh_" + side] = leg * share * (1 - knee)
        w["calf_" + side] = leg * share * knee * (1 - foot)
        w["foot_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * (1 - toe)
        w["ball_" + side] = leg * share * knee * foot * toe

    # Arms: the sleeve from the shoulder seam outwards; the jacket under the armpit stays on the spine.
    gate = ss(1.80, 1.93, z)
    arm_m = ss(0.60, 0.82, ax) * gate
    clav = 0.6 * ss(0.14, 0.42, ax) * ss(1.88, 2.08, z) * (1 - arm_m)
    scale(body, 1 - arm_m - clav)
    elbow = ss(ELBOW_X - 0.07, ELBOW_X + 0.07, ax)
    wrist = ss(WRIST_X - 0.04, WRIST_X + 0.04, ax)
    for side, m in (("l", x > 0), ("r", x <= 0)):
        w["clavicle_" + side] = clav * m
        w["upperarm_" + side] = arm_m * (1 - elbow) * m
        w["lowerarm_" + side] = arm_m * elbow * (1 - wrist) * m
        w["hand_" + side] = arm_m * wrist * m

    # Head and neck: the skin is the head; the twist is spread over the jowls and a short ring of the collar.
    out = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(head)[0], 0.4)
    inside = geodesic(co, adj, np.where(~head)[0], 0.4)
    # The skin border lies in the crease under the jowls and its texture is ragged: the first ring of black collar
    # moves with the skin, so the stretch falls on plain black shirt further out.
    reach = np.where(black, np.maximum(out - NECK_RING, 0.0), out)
    hn = np.where(head, 1.0, 1 - ss(0.0, 0.12, reach))
    w_head = np.where(head, 0.6 + 0.4 * ss(0.0, 0.10, inside), 0.6 * (1 - ss(0.0, 0.07, reach)))
    for k in names:
        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hn)
    w["head"] = w_head
    w["neck_01"] = np.maximum(hn - w_head, 0.0)

    # Tie: the gold strip on the shirt hangs from the knot on its own two bones.
    gold = (hsv[:, 0] > 0.07) & (hsv[:, 0] < 0.17) & (hsv[:, 1] > 0.45) & (hsv[:, 2] > 0.3)
    tie = gold & ~head & (ax < 0.12) & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16)
    # Dark texels inside the gold would leave holes in the strip: whatever lies inside its outline is tie as well.
    rows = np.clip(((z - 1.45) / 0.02).astype(int), 0, 35)
    half = np.zeros(36)
    np.maximum.at(half, rows[tie], ax[tie])
    half = np.maximum(half, np.maximum(np.roll(half, 1), np.roll(half, -1)))
    tie = tie | (~head & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16) & (ax < half[rows] - 0.005))
    # Notches in the outline go the same way: a vert with most of its neighbours in the tie is tie.
    for _ in range(2):
        share = np.array([tie[nb].mean() if len(nb) else 0.0 for nb in adj])
        tie = tie | (~head & (y < -0.15) & (z > 1.45) & (z < 2.16) & (share > 0.5))
    # The knot itself stays on the chest; the faces that join it to the strip must stay gold.
    knot = gold & ~tie & ~head & (ax < 0.12) & (y < -0.15) & (z > 2.0)
    hang = np.where(tie, ss(2.12, 2.00, z), 0.0)
    lower = ss(1.88, 1.72, z)
    for k in names:
        w[k] = w[k] * (1 - hang)
    w["tie_01"] = hang * (1 - lower)
    w["tie_02"] = hang * lower
    # The knot sits on the chest: it must not follow the head.
    for k in ("head", "neck_01"):
        w["spine_03"] = w["spine_03"] + np.where(tie, w[k], 0.0)
        w[k] = np.where(tie, 0.0, w[k])
    print("[build] tie verts %d" % tie.sum())

    W = np.stack([w[k] for k in names], axis=1)
    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

    # Smooth over the surface, then put the rigid parts back.
    rigid = (head & (inside > 0.08)) | (ax > WRIST_X + 0.08) | (z < 0.12) | tie
    fixed = W.copy()
    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
    for _ in range(6):
        avg = np.zeros_like(W)
        np.add.at(avg, idx, W[nbr])
        avg /= deg[:, None]
        W = 0.5 * W + 0.5 * avg
        W[rigid] = fixed[rigid]

    # Layers that lie on each other (lapel on jacket, jacket edge on shirt, tie on shirt) are not neighbours on the
    # surface, so the smoothing drives them apart: average the torso over space as well.
    # The tie is left out: it must not stick to the shirt under it.
    layered = np.where(~head & ~tie & (z > 1.15) & (ax < ELBOW_X))[0]
    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(layered))
    for k, i in enumerate(layered):
        tree.insert(co[i], k)
    tree.balance()
    near = [[layered[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_range(co[i], 0.03)] for i in layered]
    for _ in range(3):
        W[layered] = np.array([W[group].mean(axis=0) for group in near])

    # At most four influences, normalised.
    order = np.argsort(-W, axis=1)
    keep = np.zeros_like(W, dtype=bool)
    np.put_along_axis(keep, order[:, :4], True, axis=1)
    W = np.where(keep & (W > 0.01), W, 0.0)
    W = W / W.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)

    mesh.vertex_groups.clear()
    for j, name in enumerate(names):
        g = mesh.vertex_groups.new(name=name)
        col = W[:, j]
        for i in np.where(col > 0)[0]:
            g.add([int(i)], float(col[i]), "REPLACE")
    used = (W > 0).sum(axis=1)
    print("[build] influences per vertex: max %d, mean %.2f" % (used.max(), used.mean()))
    for j, name in enumerate(names):
        print("[build] group %-16s verts=%5d weight=%8.1f" % (name, (W[:, j] > 0).sum(), W[:, j].sum()))
    clean_neck_texture(mesh, adj, rgb, head, ~cream & ~tie & ~head & ~gold, inside, out)
    split_tie(mesh, co, W, names, tie, knot, black & ~tie & ~head)


def clean_neck_texture(mesh, adj, rgb, head, shirt, inside, out):
    """Make the skin-to-collar border of the base colour follow the mesh.

    Meshy paints that border across the faces, ragged, with black spilled onto the jowls and skin onto the collar; it
    shows as soon as the head turns. Near the border the faces are repainted: skin on one side of a smooth line
    over the mesh, black on the other.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    uv = np.zeros(len(me.loops) * 2, dtype=np.float32)
    me.uv_layers.active.data.foreach_get("uv", uv)
    uv = uv.reshape(-1, 2) * (w, h) - 0.5
    near_skin = head & (inside < 0.10) & (rgb.max(axis=1) > 0.4)
    tone = np.median(rgb[near_skin], axis=0)
    black_px = np.array((0.015, 0.015, 0.015))

    def is_skin(c):
        hi, lo = c.max(axis=-1), c.min(axis=-1)
        return (hi > 0.5) & ((hi - lo) > 0.2 * hi) & (c[..., 0] >= c[..., 1])

    # The border: where the skin flag, smoothed over the surface, crosses one half. Lone skin spikes in the crease
    # fall on the black side.
    side = head.astype(float)
    idx = np.array([i for i, nb in enumerate(adj) for _ in nb])
    nbr = np.array([b for nb in adj for b in nb])
    deg = np.array([max(len(nb), 1) for nb in adj], dtype=float)
    for _ in range(4):
        avg = np.zeros(len(side))
        np.add.at(avg, idx, side[nbr])
        side = 0.5 * side + 0.5 * avg / deg
    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    done = texels = 0
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        v = np.array(lt.vertices)
        hv = head[v]
        if not (band[v].any() and (hv | shirt[v]).all()):
            continue
        p = uv[np.array(lt.loops)]
        x0, y0 = np.floor(p.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
        x1, y1 = np.ceil(p.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
        if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0:
            continue
        xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
        d = (p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (p[0, 1] - p[2, 1])
        if abs(d) < 1e-9:
            continue
        b0 = ((p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
        b1 = ((p[2, 1] - p[0, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
        b2 = 1 - b0 - b1
        tol = min(0.5, 1.5 / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
        cover = (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (b2 >= -tol)
        block = px[y0:y1 + 1, x0:x1 + 1, :3]
        share = b0 * side[v[0]] + b1 * side[v[1]] + b2 * side[v[2]]
        to_skin = cover & (share > 0.5) & ~is_skin(block)
        to_black = cover & (share <= 0.5)
        own = block[cover & is_skin(block)]
        block[to_skin] = np.median(own, axis=0) if len(own) >= 4 else tone
        block[to_black] = black_px
        done += 1
        texels += int(to_skin.sum() + to_black.sum())
    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
    image.update()
    image.pack()
    print("[build] neck texture: %d faces, %d texels repainted, tone %s" % (done, texels, tone.round(3)))


def split_tie(mesh, co, W, names, tie, knot, shirt):
    """Cut the tie loose from the shirt it is modelled into.

    The tie faces are copied as a free two-sided strip that keeps the tie weights; the faces they came from stay on
    the body as plain black shirt, so nothing stretches between the two when the tie swings away. The faces that
    join the knot to the strip turn plain gold and stay where they are: black or sunk, they show as a wedge under
    the knot.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    bm.normal_update()
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    join = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and any(knot[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    held = {v for f in join for v in f.verts}
    touching = [f for f in bm.faces if any(tie[v.index] for v in f.verts) and f not in join]
    donor = next(f for f in bm.faces if all(shirt[v.index] and abs(v.co.x) > 0.15 and v.co.y < -0.2
                                             and 1.6 < v.co.z < 1.9 for v in f.verts))
    black_uv = sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)
    donor = min(faces, key=lambda f: (f.calc_center_median() - Vector(TIE_MID)).length)
    gold_uv = sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)

    def outward(v):
        """Off the chest, never sideways: the folds of the knot have walls that would slide across the strip."""
        d = Vector((0.0, min(v.normal.y, -0.3), v.normal.z))
        return d.normalized()

    front = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
    back = bmesh.ops.duplicate(bm, geom=faces)["geom"]
    for geom, lift in ((front, TIE_LIFT), (back, 0.5 * TIE_LIFT)):
        for v in geom:
            if isinstance(v, bmesh.types.BMVert):
                v.co += outward(v) * lift
    bmesh.ops.reverse_faces(bm, faces=[f for f in back if isinstance(f, bmesh.types.BMFace)])
    # The shirt under the strip sinks, so a breathing belly does not come through the tie.
    for v in {v for f in faces for v in f.verts} - held:
        v.co -= outward(v) * TIE_SINK
    # Right under the knot the strip hardly leaves the chest, and a crack between its folds must not show black.
    under = [f for f in faces if min(v.co.z for v in f.verts) > TIE_GOLD_UNDER]
    touching = [f for f in touching if f not in under]
    for group, spot in ((touching, black_uv), (join + under, gold_uv)):
        for f in group:
            for l in f.loops:
                l[uv].uv = spot
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()

    # The verts left behind move like the shirt around them.
    body = np.where(shirt)[0]
    tree = kdtree.KDTree(len(body))
    for k, i in enumerate(body):
        tree.insert(co[i], k)
    tree.balance()
    groups = [mesh.vertex_groups[name] for name in names]
    for i in np.where(tie)[0]:
        near = [body[k] for _, k, _ in tree.find_n(co[i], 6)]
        row = W[near].mean(axis=0)
        row = np.where(row >= np.sort(row)[-4], row, 0.0)
        row /= row.sum()
        for g, value in zip(groups, row):
            if value > 0:
                g.add([int(i)], float(value), "REPLACE")
            else:
                g.remove([int(i)])
    print("[build] tie split: %d faces copied twice, %d turned black, %d gold under the knot, %d verts in all" % (
        len(faces), len(touching), len(join), len(me.vertices)))


def clean_actions(arm):
    """Meshy names are 'Armature|Idle'; curves of the dropped bones and of the armature object itself go."""
    bones = {b.name for b in arm.data.bones}
    for action in list(bpy.data.actions):
        action.name = action.name.split("|")[-1]

def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    arm, mesh = import_source()
    weld(mesh)
    me = mesh.data
    co = np.zeros(len(me.vertices) * 3)
    me.vertices.foreach_get("co", co)
    co = co.reshape(-1, 3)
    print("[build] welded verts %d, bbox %s %s" % (len(co), co.min(axis=0).round(3), co.max(axis=0).round(3)))
    joints, toe_dir, ball_xy = measure(co)
    refit_skeleton(arm, joints)
    paint(mesh, arm, toe_dir, ball_xy)
    clean_actions(arm)
    # The Meshy clips keyed the armature object itself at 90 degrees; with those curves gone it stays upright.
    arm.animation_data.action = None
    arm.location = (0, 0, 0)
    arm.rotation_euler = (0, 0, 0)
    arm.rotation_quaternion = (1, 0, 0, 0)
    arm.scale = (1, 1, 1)
    for pb in arm.pose.bones:

    bpy.context.scene.render.fps = 30
    try:
        bpy.ops.file.pack_all()
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print("[build] pack_all:", e)
    bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath=OUT)
    print("[build] saved", OUT)

Face kind: green repainted, red not repainted, blue a face made by the tie split. Side field is grey, 0.5 is the border.
  blender -b --python neck_probe.py -- clips.blend debug.npz out.png Idle 17 front|q3|q3r|side
"""
import math
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector
from mathutils.interpolate import poly_3d_calc

path, dbg, out, clip, frame, view = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:][:6]
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
ob = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
data = np.load(dbg)
side, hit = data["side"], set(int(i) for i in data["hit"])
n_side = len(side)
if clip != "rest":
    action = bpy.data.actions[clip]
    if arm.animation_data is None:
        arm.animation_data_create()
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    if hasattr(arm.animation_data, "action_slot") and getattr(action, "slots", None):
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    bpy.context.scene.frame_set(int(frame))
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
ev = ob.evaluated_get(dg)
me = ev.data
img = next(n.image for m in me.materials for n in m.node_tree.nodes
           if n.type == "TEX_IMAGE" and n.image and n.outputs[0].links
           and any(l.to_socket.name == "Base Color" for l in n.outputs[0].links))
w, h = img.size
px = np.empty(w * h * 4, dtype=np.float32)
img.pixels.foreach_get(px)
px = px.reshape(h, w, 4)
uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
target = arm.matrix_world @ arm.pose.bones["neck_01"].head
az = {"front": 0.0, "q3": 38.0, "q3r": -38.0, "side": 90.0}[view]
el = math.radians(8.0)
a = math.radians(az)
d = Vector((-math.sin(a) * math.cos(el), -math.cos(a) * math.cos(el), math.sin(el))).normalized()
right = Vector((0, 0, 1)).cross(d).normalized()
up = d.cross(right).normalized()
if up.z < 0:
    up = -up
if right.dot(Vector((math.cos(a), -math.sin(a), 0))) < 0:
    right = -right
N, scale = 320, 0.5
pic = np.zeros((N, 3 * N, 4), dtype=np.float32)
pic[..., 3] = 1
for j in range(N):
    for i in range(N):
        o = target + d * 3.0 + right * ((i + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale + up * ((j + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale
        ok, loc, nor, fi = ev.ray_cast(o, -d)
        if not ok:
            pic[j, i, :3] = pic[j, N + i, :3] = pic[j, 2 * N + i, :3] = (0.3, 0.3, 0.4)
            continue
        f = me.polygons[fi]
        bw = poly_3d_calc([me.vertices[k].co for k in f.vertices], loc)
        c = sum((uv[l].uv * b for l, b in zip(f.loop_indices, bw)), Vector((0, 0)))
        pic[j, i, :3] = px[min(int(c.y % 1 * h), h - 1), min(int(c.x % 1 * w), w - 1), :3]
        if all(k < n_side for k in f.vertices):
            s = sum(side[k] * b for k, b in zip(f.vertices, bw))
            pic[j, N + i, :3] = (1.0, 0.6, 0.2) if abs(s - 0.5) < 0.03 else (s, s, s)
            pic[j, 2 * N + i, :3] = (0, 0.8, 0) if fi in hit else (0.8, 0, 0)
        else:
            pic[j, N + i, :3] = pic[j, 2 * N + i, :3] = (0, 0, 0.8)
res = bpy.data.images.new("ray", 3 * N, N)
res.pixels.foreach_set(pic.ravel())
res.filepath_raw = out
res.file_format = "PNG"
res.save()
print("ok polys", len(me.polygons), "side", n_side)

def smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, band):
    """The skin flag of each vert near the border, averaged over the surface around it by area.

    One half of that field is a border that does not follow the edges of the mesh, however uneven the faces are.
    """
    area = np.zeros(len(co))
    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        for k in lt.vertices:
            if k < len(co):
                area[k] += lt.area / 3
    flag = head.astype(float)
    side = flag.copy()
    for i in np.where(band)[0]:
        d = geodesic(co, adj, [i], 3 * NECK_BLUR)
        near = np.where(d < 3 * NECK_BLUR)[0]
        weight = area[near] * np.exp(-0.5 * (d[near] / NECK_BLUR) ** 2)
        if weight.sum() > 0:
            side[i] = (weight * flag[near]).sum() / weight.sum()
    # A vert right on the border would make faces that lie on both sides.
    return np.where(np.abs(side - 0.5) < 1e-3, 0.501, side)


def plain_black_uv(bm, uv, shirt):
    """One texel of plain black shirt, far from any seam."""
    donor = next(f for f in bm.faces if all(v.index < len(shirt) and shirt[v.index] and abs(v.co.x) > 0.15
                                             and v.co.y < -0.2 and 1.6 < v.co.z < 1.9 for v in f.verts))
    return sum((l[uv].uv for l in donor.loops), Vector((0, 0))) / len(donor.loops)


def covered(p, w, h, tol):
    """Texels under a UV triangle given in texel units: the slices of the block and the mask inside it."""
    x0, y0 = np.floor(p.min(axis=0)).astype(int) - 1
    x1, y1 = np.ceil(p.max(axis=0)).astype(int) + 1
    x0, y0, x1, y1 = max(x0, 0), max(y0, 0), min(x1, w - 1), min(y1, h - 1)
    d = (p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (p[0, 1] - p[2, 1])
    if x1 < x0 or y1 < y0 or abs(d) < 1e-9:
        return None
    xs, ys = np.meshgrid(np.arange(x0, x1 + 1), np.arange(y0, y1 + 1))
    b0 = ((p[1, 1] - p[2, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[2, 0] - p[1, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
    b1 = ((p[2, 1] - p[0, 1]) * (xs - p[2, 0]) + (p[0, 0] - p[2, 0]) * (ys - p[2, 1])) / d
    tol = min(0.5, tol / max(x1 - x0, y1 - y0, 1))
    return slice(y0, y1 + 1), slice(x0, x1 + 1), (b0 >= -tol) & (b1 >= -tol) & (1 - b0 - b1 >= -tol)


def neck_border(mesh, co, adj, rgb, head, shirt, black_shirt, inside, out):
    """Cut a clean skin-to-collar border into the mesh.

    Meshy paints that border across the faces, ragged, with black spilled onto the jowls and skin onto the collar,
    and the faces in the crease are slivers with a few stretched texels each: it shows as a hairy fringe as soon as
    the head turns. The faces near the border are cut along a smooth line over the surface; on the collar side they
    turn plain black, on the skin side whatever is not skin is painted over.
    """
    me = mesh.data
    n = len(head)
    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, band)
    near_skin = head & (inside < 0.10) & (rgb.max(axis=1) > 0.4)
    tone = np.median(rgb[near_skin], axis=0)

    def is_skin(c):
        hi, lo = c.max(axis=-1), c.min(axis=-1)
        return (hi > 0.5) & ((hi - lo) > 0.2 * hi) & (c[..., 0] >= c[..., 1])

    bm = bmesh.new()
    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
    black_uv = plain_black_uv(bm, uv, black_shirt)
    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.index < n and (head[v.index] or shirt[v.index]) for v in f.verts)
             and any(band[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    value = {v: float(side[v.index]) for f in faces for v in f.verts}
    fresh = set()
    for e in {e for f in faces for e in f.edges}:
        a, b = e.verts
        sa, sb = value[a], value[b]
        if (sa - 0.5) * (sb - 0.5) >= 0:
            continue
        t = min(max((0.5 - sa) / (sb - sa), 0.05), 0.95)
        where = a.co.lerp(b.co, t)
        v = bmesh.utils.edge_split(e, a, t)[1]
        if (v.co - where).length > 1e-5:
            raise RuntimeError("edge_split measures from the other end")
        value[v] = 0.5
        fresh.add(v)
    # Each cut face gets an edge along the border; a neighbour that only received a vert is closed with a fan.
    for f in list({f for v in fresh for f in v.link_faces}):
        on = [v for v in f.verts if v in fresh]
        if len(on) == 2:
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], on[1])
        elif len(on) == 1 and len(f.verts) == 4:
            ring = list(f.verts)
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], ring[(ring.index(on[0]) + 2) % 4])
    bmesh.ops.triangulate(bm, faces=list({f for v in fresh for f in v.link_faces if len(f.verts) > 3}))

    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    skin, collar = [], []
    for f in {f for v in value for f in v.link_faces}:
        if all(v in value for v in f.verts) and any(v in fresh or band[v.index] for v in f.verts):
            (skin if sum(value[v] for v in f.verts) / len(f.verts) > 0.5 else collar).append(f)
    texels = 0
    # The collar faces leave their texels; next to the border those texels still bleed into the skin faces.
    for f in collar:
        if any(v in fresh for v in f.verts):
            hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
            if hit:
                block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
                block[hit[2]] = tone
        for l in f.loops:
            l[uv].uv = black_uv
    for f in skin:
        hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
        if hit:
            block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
            own = block[hit[2] & is_skin(block)]
            wrong = hit[2] & ~is_skin(block)
            block[wrong] = np.median(own, axis=0) if len(own) >= 4 else tone
            texels += int(wrong.sum())
    first = len(me.vertices)
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()
    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
    image.update()
    image.pack()

    # A vert made by the cut carries the weights of both ends of its edge: back to four influences.
    for i in range(first, len(me.vertices)):
        groups = sorted(me.vertices[i].groups, key=lambda g: -g.weight)
        total = sum(g.weight for g in groups[:4])
        for k, g in enumerate([(g.group, g.weight) for g in groups]):
            if k < 4:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].add([i], g[1] / total, "REPLACE")
            else:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].remove([i])
    print("[build] neck border: %d verts cut in, %d skin faces, %d collar faces turned black, %d texels to skin, "
          "tone %s, %d verts in all" % (len(me.vertices) - first, len(skin), len(collar), texels, tone.round(3),
                                        len(me.vertices)))

    near_skin = head & (inside < 0.10) & (rgb.max(axis=1) > 0.4)
    tone = np.median(rgb[near_skin], axis=0)

    def is_skin(c):
        hi, lo = c.max(axis=-1), c.min(axis=-1)
        return (hi > 0.5) & ((hi - lo) > 0.2 * hi) & (c[..., 0] >= c[..., 1])

    bm.from_mesh(me)
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    uv = bm.loops.layers.uv.active
    black_uv = plain_black_uv(bm, uv, black_shirt)
    faces = [f for f in bm.faces if all(v.index < n and (head[v.index] or shirt[v.index]) for v in f.verts)
             and any(band[v.index] for v in f.verts)]
    value = {v: float(side[v.index]) for f in faces for v in f.verts}
    fresh = set()
    for e in {e for f in faces for e in f.edges}:
        a, b = e.verts
        sa, sb = value[a], value[b]
        if (sa - 0.5) * (sb - 0.5) >= 0:
            continue
        t = min(max((0.5 - sa) / (sb - sa), 0.05), 0.95)
        where = a.co.lerp(b.co, t)
        v = bmesh.utils.edge_split(e, a, t)[1]
        if (v.co - where).length > 1e-5:
            raise RuntimeError("edge_split measures from the other end")
        value[v] = 0.5
        fresh.add(v)

    for f in list({f for v in fresh for f in v.link_faces}):
        on = [v for v in f.verts if v in fresh]
        if len(on) == 2:
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], on[1])
        elif len(on) == 1 and len(f.verts) == 4:
            ring = list(f.verts)
            bmesh.utils.face_split(f, on[0], ring[(ring.index(on[0]) + 2) % 4])

    image = base_image(me)
    w, h = image.size
    px = np.array(image.pixels[:], dtype=np.float32).reshape(h, w, 4)
    size = np.array((w, h))
    skin, collar = [], []
    for f in {f for v in value for f in v.link_faces}:
        if all(v in value for v in f.verts) and any(v in fresh or band[v.index] for v in f.verts):
            (skin if sum(value[v] for v in f.verts) / len(f.verts) > 0.5 else collar).append(f)
    texels = 0
    # The collar faces leave their texels; next to the border those texels still bleed into the skin faces.
    for f in collar:
        if any(v in fresh for v in f.verts):
            hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
            if hit:
                block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
                block[hit[2]] = tone
        for l in f.loops:
            l[uv].uv = black_uv
    for f in skin:
        hit = covered(np.array([l[uv].uv[:] for l in f.loops]) * size - 0.5, w, h, 1.5)
        if hit:
            block = px[hit[0], hit[1], :3]
            own = block[hit[2] & is_skin(block)]
            wrong = hit[2] & ~is_skin(block)
            block[wrong] = np.median(own, axis=0) if len(own) >= 4 else tone
            texels += int(wrong.sum())
    first = len(me.vertices)
    bm.to_mesh(me)
    bm.free()
    image.pixels.foreach_set(px.ravel())
    image.update()
    image.pack()

    # A vert made by the cut carries the weights of both ends of its edge: back to four influences.
    for i in range(first, len(me.vertices)):
        groups = sorted(me.vertices[i].groups, key=lambda g: -g.weight)
        total = sum(g.weight for g in groups[:4])
        for k, g in enumerate([(g.group, g.weight) for g in groups]):
            if k < 4:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].add([i], g[1] / total, "REPLACE")
            else:
                mesh.vertex_groups[g[0]].remove([i])
    print("[build] neck border: %d verts cut in, %d skin faces, %d collar faces turned black, %d texels to skin, "
          "tone %s, %d verts in all" % (len(me.vertices) - first, len(skin), len(collar), texels, tone.round(3),
                                        len(me.vertices)))

"""Ray-cast picture of a pose, three panels: texel colour, depth with face normals, one colour per face.

  blender -b --python geo_probe.py -- clips.blend out.png Idle 17 front dx dy scale
dx, dy move the centre from the head of neck_01, in metres on the screen.
"""
import math
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector
from mathutils.interpolate import poly_3d_calc

path, out, clip, frame, view, dx, dy, scale = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:][:8]
dx, dy, scale = float(dx), float(dy), float(scale)
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
ob = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
if clip != "rest":
    action = bpy.data.actions[clip]
    if arm.animation_data is None:
        arm.animation_data_create()
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    if hasattr(arm.animation_data, "action_slot") and getattr(action, "slots", None):
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    bpy.context.scene.frame_set(int(frame))
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
ev = ob.evaluated_get(dg)
me = ev.data
img = next(n.image for m in me.materials for n in m.node_tree.nodes
           if n.type == "TEX_IMAGE" and n.image and n.outputs[0].links
           and any(l.to_socket.name == "Base Color" for l in n.outputs[0].links))
w, h = img.size
px = np.empty(w * h * 4, dtype=np.float32)
img.pixels.foreach_get(px)
px = px.reshape(h, w, 4)
uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
az = {"front": 0.0, "q3": 38.0, "q3r": -38.0, "side": 90.0}[view]
el = math.radians(8.0)
a = math.radians(az)
d = Vector((-math.sin(a) * math.cos(el), -math.cos(a) * math.cos(el), math.sin(el))).normalized()
right = Vector((0, 0, 1)).cross(d).normalized()
up = d.cross(right).normalized()
if up.z < 0:
    up = -up
if right.dot(Vector((math.cos(a), -math.sin(a), 0))) < 0:
    right = -right
target = arm.matrix_world @ arm.pose.bones["neck_01"].head + right * dx + up * dy
N = 560
pic = np.zeros((N, 3 * N, 4), dtype=np.float32)
pic[..., 3] = 1
depth = np.full((N, N), np.nan)
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
tint = rng.random((len(me.polygons), 3)) * 0.7 + 0.3
for j in range(N):
    for i in range(N):
        o = target + d * 3.0 + right * ((i + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale + up * ((j + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale
        ok, loc, nor, fi = ev.ray_cast(o, -d)
        if not ok:
            continue
        f = me.polygons[fi]
        bw = poly_3d_calc([me.vertices[k].co for k in f.vertices], loc)
        c = sum((uv[l].uv * b for l, b in zip(f.loop_indices, bw)), Vector((0, 0)))
        col = px[min(int(c.y % 1 * h), h - 1), min(int(c.x % 1 * w), w - 1), :3]
        pic[j, i, :3] = col

"""Which band faces of the built rig have a collapsed UV, against the side of their verts."""
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np

path, dbg = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:][:2]
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
ob = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
me = ob.data
data = np.load(dbg)
side, head, band, shirt = data["side"], data["head"], data["band"], data["shirt"]
n = len(side)
uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
print("verts", len(me.vertices), "n", n, "polys", len(me.polygons))
stats = {}
for f in me.polygons:
    vs = list(f.vertices)
    if not all(k < n for k in vs):
        if all(k < n or k >= 13168 for k in vs) and any(k >= 13168 for k in vs):
            kind = "cut face"
        else:
            continue
    elif all(head[k] or shirt[k] for k in vs) and any(band[k] for k in vs):
        m = np.mean([side[k] for k in vs])
        kind = "whole skin" if m > 0.5 else "whole collar"
    else:
        continue
    p = np.array([uv[l].uv[:] for l in f.loop_indices])
    flat = np.abs(p - p[0]).max() < 1e-6
    key = (kind, bool(flat))
    stats[key] = stats.get(key, 0) + 1
for k, v in sorted(stats.items()):
    print(k, v)
# The mesh the side field was computed on against the saved one.
co = np.array([v.co[:] for v in me.vertices[:n]])
print("head verts z range", co[head[:n]][:, 2].min().round(3), co[head[:n]][:, 2].max().round(3))
print("side>0.5 & ~head", int(((side > 0.5) & ~head).sum()), "side<0.5 & head", int(((side < 0.5) & head).sum()))

import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()


def swap(old, new_text):
    global text
    assert text.count(old) == 1, old
    text = text.replace(old, new_text)


swap('''# Faces within this distance (m) of the skin border get their texture cleaned.
NECK_BAND = 0.10
# Width of the average that draws the skin-to-collar border.
NECK_BLUR = 0.025
''', '''# Faces within this distance (m) of the painted skin border are cut and cleaned.
NECK_BAND = 0.10
# Width (m) of the average that draws the new skin-to-collar border; it stays within NECK_REACH of the painted one.
NECK_BLUR = 0.045
NECK_REACH = 0.06
''')
a = text.index("def smooth_side(")
b = text.index("def plain_black_uv(")
text = text[:a] + '''def smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, close):
    """The skin flag of each vert close to the border, averaged over the surface around it by area.

    One half of that field is a border that does not follow the edges of the mesh, however uneven the faces are.
    """
    area = np.zeros(len(co))
    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        for k in lt.vertices:
            if k < len(co):
                area[k] += lt.area / 3
    span = [[float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b])) for b in nb] for a, nb in enumerate(adj)]
    limit = 2.5 * NECK_BLUR
    side = head.astype(float)
    for i in np.where(close)[0]:
        dist = {int(i): 0.0}
        heap = [(0.0, int(i))]
        while heap:
            d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if d > dist[a]:
                continue
            for b, step in zip(adj[a], span[a]):
                nd = d + step
                if nd < limit and nd < dist.get(b, limit):
                    dist[b] = nd
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
        near = np.fromiter(dist.keys(), dtype=np.int64)
        weight = area[near] * np.exp(-0.5 * (np.fromiter(dist.values(), dtype=float) / NECK_BLUR) ** 2)
        side[i] = (weight * head[near]).sum() / weight.sum()
    # A vert right on the border would make faces that lie on both sides.
    return np.where(np.abs(side - 0.5) < 1e-3, 0.501, side)


''' + text[b:]
swap('''    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, band)
''', '''    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_REACH)
''')
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(text)
print("ok")

@RTK.md

# Рабочий флоу по умолчанию

Структурированный флоу — это: обсуждение → грил (/grilling) → тикеты → реализация через TDD (/tdd, красный-зелёный на согласованных швах).

Перед стартом каждой НОВОЙ задачи (не подзадачи текущей) реши, нужен ли он:

- **Уверен, что флоу не нужен** — скипай молча, не спрашивая, и сразу берись за работу. Это про мелкие правки, однострочники, операционные и разведочные действия, ответы на вопросы, правку конфигов и доков.
- **Уверен, что нужен, или сомневаешься** — спроси одним коротким вопросом, каким именно флоу вести (полный / только обсуждение + грил / без флоу). Задал вопрос — жди ответа, не начинай работу до него.

Для чисто исследовательских и операционных задач без производственного кода (разведка API, генерация контента, публикация) в вопросе сразу отметь, что TDD-часть там применить не к чему — уместны только обсуждение и грил.

# Бюджет лимитов: прогноз перед тяжёлым запуском

Перед любым запуском, который может съесть заметную часть 5-часового лимита, сначала
напиши в чат прогноз и жди моего явного «да». Тяжёлым считается: Workflow (любой),
больше 3 субагентов разом или в цикле, фоновые агенты на длинные задачи. Правило
действует всегда, в том числе в ultracode-сессиях: ultracode разрешает workflow, но не
отменяет прогноз и подтверждение.

В прогнозе:
- сколько агентов (с учётом верификаторов и циклов, худший случай);
- грубая оценка токенов (ориентир: агент-исследователь 50-150k, Opus дороже Sonnet);
- примерная доля 5-часового лимита и время;
- дешёвый вариант (меньше агентов, Sonnet или Haiku, без верификации) рядом с полным.

Хук `workflow-guard` на каждый Workflow запрашивает моё подтверждение, но прогноз
в чате должен прийти до вызова, а не вместо него. Если запуск уже идёт и расход
растёт быстрее прогноза, остановись и скажи.

# Стиль письма

**Длинные тире.** По умолчанию ставь запятую, двоеточие или скобки там, где
напрашивается «—». Тире оставляй для настоящего разрыва мысли, и не чаще одного
раза на длинный текст. Правило касается всего, что пишешь ты: ответы в терминале,
комментарии к PR и ревью, сообщения коммитов, документация, отчёты. Мой
собственный текст не переписывай, если об этом не просили.

**Язык в коде, коммитах и пул-реквестах.** Комментарии в коде, сообщения коммитов
(git и dv), комментарии, ревью и описания PR всегда по-английски, даже если
окружающий код прокомментирован по-русски или коллега в треде пишет по-русски.
Старые русские комментарии не переводи, если об этом не просили. Разговор со мной
в терминале, наоборот, по-русски.


# Shell и деструктивные операции

- **Никаких heredoc и многострочных строк с backslash-экранированием в Bash.** Всё
  многострочное (скрипты, JSON, тексты) пишется в файл через Write, потом файл
  исполняется или читается. Хук `bash-guard` блокирует heredoc автоматически.
- **Деструктивные операции** (rm -rf, drop, truncate, delete from, firestore delete,
  git clean и т.п.) только через скрипт-файл с флагом `--dry-run`, включённым по
  умолчанию. Сначала прогон в dry-run с точными счётчиками, потом остановка и
  ожидание моего явного «да». Хук переводит такие команды в режим подтверждения.
- Перед `git push`: перейти в корень репозитория и показать `pwd`.

# Проверяй, прежде чем утверждать

- Любое утверждение о нашем коде, PR, стороннем API, статусе внешнего сервиса или
  игровой механике сначала проверяется по источнику: файл, документация, ответ API.
  В ответе указывай, что именно проверено и где.
- Если проверить нельзя, пиши «не проверено» явно, а не утверждай.

# Формат ответов

- По умолчанию коротко: сначала ответ, потом детали, если нужны. Не пересказывай
  мне мой же план обратно.
- Первая строка ответа: сам ответ или действие. Без вступлений вроде «Сейчас
  сделаю…», «Отличный вопрос».
- В конце одно конкретное следующее действие (моё или твоё), если что-то
  осталось открытым. Без «обращайся, если что».
- Без пересказа сделанного после задачи: только что теперь работает и что
  проверено.
- Списки до 5 пунктов. Больше: сгруппируй и поставь важное первым, остальное
  отдай по запросу.
- Ответ в чате читается за 10-20 секунд. Большой материал (список тикетов,
  таблица, план на десятки пунктов) не вываливай в чат: пиши в файл, в чат
  дай сводку из 3-5 строк и путь.
- В многошаговой работе пиши, где мы: «шаг 3 из 5: …, дальше …».
- Правила из «Проверяй, прежде чем утверждать» и саммари к текстам остаются
  в силе: краткость их не отменяет.
  (Основано на скилле ayghri/i-have-adhd, принято на постоянку 2026-11-01.)
- Тексты для Slack, Telegram, почты и клиентов: только plain text, без
  markdown-таблиц и заголовков, до 5 строк, если я не просил больше.

# Коммуникации: отправка только по моему прямому указанию

- В Slack, почту, мессенджеры и подобные каналы ты отправляешь только тогда,
  когда я прямо попросил отправить именно это сообщение в текущем разговоре.
  По собственной инициативе никогда: по умолчанию ты готовишь текст, вставляю
  и отправляю я. Хук `comms-guard` на каждую отправку (сообщение, файл в канал,
  письмо) запрашивает моё подтверждение. Комментарии и ревью в PR это не
  касается.
- К каждому подготовленному тексту прилагай короткое саммари на русском
  (1-3 строки): кому, о чём, что важно. Сам текст на языке адресата.

# Дисциплина скоупа

- Ревью, аудит, написание тикетов: на выходе только находки и тикеты. Правки
  только после явного «implement» / «сделай».
- Не добавляй в план пункты, которых я не просил. Помечай их как необязательные
  предложения отдельным списком.

# RTK - Rust Token Killer

**Usage**: Token-optimized CLI proxy (60-90% savings on dev operations)

## Meta Commands (always use rtk directly)

```bash
rtk gain              # Show token savings analytics
rtk gain --history    # Show command usage history with savings
rtk discover          # Analyze Claude Code history for missed opportunities
rtk proxy <cmd>       # Execute raw command without filtering (for debugging)
```

## Installation Verification

```bash
rtk --version         # Should show: rtk X.Y.Z
rtk gain              # Should work (not "command not found")
which rtk             # Verify correct binary
```

⚠️ **Name collision**: If `rtk gain` fails, you may have reachingforthejack/rtk (Rust Type Kit) installed instead.

## Hook-Based Usage

All other commands are automatically rewritten by the Claude Code hook.
Example: `git status` → `rtk git status` (transparent, 0 tokens overhead)

Refer to CLAUDE.md for full command reference.

# MegaJam 2026: project rules

Everything is in **English**: the conversation with the author, code, comments, commits, the dev log and every text
in the game (jam rule: the submission must be playable and judged in English; the session logs are part of the dev
log). The author may write in Russian; reply in English anyway.

## Hard rules

1. **Jam window: 2026-11-12 05:00 UTC to 2026-11-16 01:59 UTC.** Everything in the game (gameplay code, levels,
   art, sound) is made inside it. Before the start only tooling exists: see `PREJAM.md`. Rules and deadlines are in
   `JAM_BRIEF.md`.
2. **Engine: UE 5.8**, module `JamGame`, tests `Jam.<Area>.<Case>`, log category `LogJamGame`.
3. **Build and tests: `bash Tools/Build/build_and_test.sh`.** The script closes only this project's editor, the full
   build needs no permission. New `check_code.py` warnings are fixed or justified in one line.
4. **The MCP server of this project is on port 8002** (Diskworld 8000, CastleFight 8001).
5. **Version control: git + LFS.** Commit after Save All in the editor, otherwise an old `.uasset` gets in. Never
   amend: each commit is evidence of when the work was done.
6. **Agent logs are part of the submission evidence.** `Tools/Git/hooks/pre-commit` exports every Claude Code
   session of this project to `_AgentLogs/` on each commit. Enable once per clone:
   `git config core.hooksPath Tools/Git/hooks`. A session run from another folder is listed in
   `Tools/Devlog/sessions.json`.
7. **Third-party content is declared.** Every asset, plugin, model or sound that the team did not make during the
   jam goes to `THIRD_PARTY.md` with its source and licence at the moment it is added.
8. **Deleting files** only through a script with a dry run by default and the author's explicit yes.

## Working cycle

- Production code is written test-first: a `Jam.` test before the code, decisions in pure `*Rules`
  (`.claude/rules/cpp.md`).
- Packaging: `bash Tools/Build/package.sh --config Shipping --name TeamName_GameName`, then
  `bash Tools/Build/smoke_package.sh`. Warn the author before a smoke run: it opens a game window.
- The dev log is `DEVLOG.md`: a few lines per working block (what was done, which AI tool, what went wrong).
- [Aim feel reference](aim-feel-reference.md) — Hades 2: instant turn to the mouse, visible cursor, no crosshair

  мне мой же план обратно.
- Первая строка ответа: сам ответ или действие. Без вступлений вроде «Сейчас
  сделаю…», «Отличный вопрос».
- В конце одно конкретное следующее действие (моё или твоё), если что-то
  осталось открытым. Без «обращайся, если что».
- Без пересказа сделанного после задачи: только что теперь работает и что
  проверено.
- Списки до 5 пунктов. Больше: сгруппируй и поставь важное первым, остальное
  отдай по запросу.
- Ответ в чате читается за 10-20 секунд. Большой материал (список тикетов,
  таблица, план на десятки пунктов) не вываливай в чат: пиши в файл, в чат
  дай сводку из 3-5 строк и путь.
- В многошаговой работе пиши, где мы: «шаг 3 из 5: …, дальше …».
- Правила из «Проверяй, прежде чем утверждать» и саммари к текстам остаются

"""Round 8: the border field is a signed distance, and faces that reach the jacket are cut as well."""
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()


def swap(old, new_text):
    global text
    assert text.count(old) == 1, old
    text = text.replace(old, new_text)


swap('''def smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, close):
    """The skin flag of each vert close to the border, averaged over the surface around it by area.

    One half of that field is a border that does not follow the edges of the mesh, however uneven the faces are.
    """
''', '''def border_distance(me, co, adj, head, signed):
    """Distance (m) of each vert from a smooth skin-to-collar border, positive on the skin.

    Close to the painted border the skin flag is averaged over the surface by area; across a straight border that

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Rebuild with the debug dump, the neck close-ups and two side probes.
#   bash rbsp.sh <tag>
set -uo pipefail
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
R=/f/Unreal_Engine/UnrealProjects/MegaJam2026
B="/f/Program Files/Blender Foundation/Blender 5.2/blender.exe"
F="$R/Art/Models/boss_fixed/publisher_clips.blend"
TAG="$1"
cd "$R"
PUBLISHER_DEBUG="$S/dbg_$TAG.npz" bash Tools/Art/publisher_rig/rebuild.sh "$S/rb_$TAG" > "$S/rb_$TAG.out" 2>&1
grep -n "Error\|Traceback" "$S/rb_$TAG/"*.log "$S/rb_$TAG.out"
grep -n "neck border\|tie split" "$S/rb_$TAG.out"
"$B" -b --factory-startup --python "$S/side_probe.py" -- "$F" "$S/dbg_$TAG.npz" "$S/sp_${TAG}_a.png" Idle 17 front -0.15 0.13 0.22 > "$S/sp_$TAG.log" 2>&1
"$B" -b --factory-startup --python "$S/side_probe.py" -- "$F" "$S/dbg_$TAG.npz" "$S/sp_${TAG}_b.png" Hit_Reaction 17 side 0.12 0.15 0.3 >> "$S/sp_$TAG.log" 2>&1
grep -n "Error\|Traceback" "$S/sp_$TAG.log"
bash "$S/nq.sh" "$TAG"

"""Round 8: a wider average for the neck border, with its own fast walk over the surface."""
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()


def swap(old, new_text):
    global text
    assert text.count(old) == 1, old
    text = text.replace(old, new_text)


swap('''# Faces within this distance (m) of the skin border get their texture cleaned.
NECK_BAND = 0.10
# Width of the average that draws the skin-to-collar border.
NECK_BLUR = 0.025
''', '''# Faces within this distance (m) of the painted skin border are cut and cleaned.
NECK_BAND = 0.10
# Width (m) of the average that draws the new skin-to-collar border; it stays within NECK_REACH of the painted one.
NECK_BLUR = 0.045
NECK_REACH = 0.06
''')
a = text.index("def smooth_side(")
b = text.index("def plain_black_uv(")
text = text[:a] + '''def smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, close):
    """The skin flag of each vert close to the border, averaged over the surface around it by area.

    One half of that field is a border that does not follow the edges of the mesh, however uneven the faces are.
    """
    area = np.zeros(len(co))
    me.calc_loop_triangles()
    for lt in me.loop_triangles:
        for k in lt.vertices:
            if k < len(co):
                area[k] += lt.area / 3
    span = [[float(np.linalg.norm(co[a] - co[b])) for b in nb] for a, nb in enumerate(adj)]
    limit = 2.5 * NECK_BLUR
    side = head.astype(float)
    for i in np.where(close)[0]:
        dist = {int(i): 0.0}
        heap = [(0.0, int(i))]
        while heap:
            d, a = heapq.heappop(heap)
            if d > dist[a]:
                continue
            for b, step in zip(adj[a], span[a]):
                nd = d + step
                if nd < limit and nd < dist.get(b, limit):
                    dist[b] = nd
                    heapq.heappush(heap, (nd, b))
        near = np.fromiter(dist.keys(), dtype=np.int64)
        weight = area[near] * np.exp(-0.5 * (np.fromiter(dist.values(), dtype=float) / NECK_BLUR) ** 2)
        side[i] = (weight * head[near]).sum() / weight.sum()
    # A vert right on the border would make faces that lie on both sides.
    return np.where(np.abs(side - 0.5) < 1e-3, 0.501, side)


''' + text[b:]
swap('''    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, band)
''', '''    band = np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_BAND
    side = smooth_side(me, co, adj, head, np.where(head, inside, out) < NECK_REACH)
''')
open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n").write(text)
print("ok")

"""Ray-cast picture of a pose, three panels: texel colour, the side field, the kind of the verts.

Panel 3: red = raw head flag, green = in the band, blue = neither skin nor shirt (a face with one is not cut).
Verts made by the tie split or by the cut have no record: they show as 0.5 / grey.
  blender -b --python side_probe.py -- clips.blend debug.npz out.png Idle 17 front dx dy scale
"""
import math
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector
from mathutils.interpolate import poly_3d_calc

path, dbg, out, clip, frame, view, dx, dy, scale = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:][:9]
dx, dy, scale = float(dx), float(dy), float(scale)
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
ob = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
data = np.load(dbg)
side, head, band, shirt = data["side"], data["head"], data["band"], data["shirt"]
n = len(side)
if clip != "rest":
    action = bpy.data.actions[clip]
    if arm.animation_data is None:
        arm.animation_data_create()
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    if hasattr(arm.animation_data, "action_slot") and getattr(action, "slots", None):
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    bpy.context.scene.frame_set(int(frame))
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
ev = ob.evaluated_get(dg)
me = ev.data
img = next(nd.image for m in me.materials for nd in m.node_tree.nodes
           if nd.type == "TEX_IMAGE" and nd.image and nd.outputs[0].links
           and any(l.to_socket.name == "Base Color" for l in nd.outputs[0].links))
w, h = img.size
px = np.empty(w * h * 4, dtype=np.float32)
img.pixels.foreach_get(px)
px = px.reshape(h, w, 4)
uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
az = {"front": 0.0, "q3": 38.0, "q3r": -38.0, "side": 90.0}[view]
el = math.radians(8.0)
a = math.radians(az)
d = Vector((-math.sin(a) * math.cos(el), -math.cos(a) * math.cos(el), math.sin(el))).normalized()
right = Vector((0, 0, 1)).cross(d).normalized()
up = d.cross(right).normalized()
if up.z < 0:
    up = -up
if right.dot(Vector((math.cos(a), -math.sin(a), 0))) < 0:
    right = -right
target = arm.matrix_world @ arm.pose.bones["neck_01"].head + right * dx + up * dy
N = 560
pic = np.zeros((N, 3 * N, 4), dtype=np.float32)
pic[..., 3] = 1
for j in range(N):
    for i in range(N):
        o = target + d * 3.0 + right * ((i + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale + up * ((j + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale
        ok, loc, nor, fi = ev.ray_cast(o, -d)
        if not ok:
            continue
        f = me.polygons[fi]
        bw = poly_3d_calc([me.vertices[k].co for k in f.vertices], loc)
        c = sum((uv[l].uv * b for l, b in zip(f.loop_indices, bw)), Vector((0, 0)))
        pic[j, i, :3] = px[min(int(c.y % 1 * h), h - 1), min(int(c.x % 1 * w), w - 1), :3]
        s = sum((side[k] if k < n else 0.5) * b for k, b in zip(f.vertices, bw))
        edge = min(bw) < 0.03
        pic[j, N + i, :3] = (1.0, 0.6, 0.2) if abs(s - 0.5) < 0.02 else ((s * 0.8, s * 0.8, s * 0.8 + 0.2) if edge else (s, s, s))
        kind = np.zeros(3)
        for k, b in zip(f.vertices, bw):
            if k < n:
                kind += b * np.array((float(head[k]), float(band[k]), float(not (head[k] or shirt[k]))))
            else:
                kind += b * np.array((0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
        pic[j, 2 * N + i, :3] = kind * (0.7 if edge else 1.0)
res = bpy.data.images.new("ray", 3 * N, N)
res.pixels.foreach_set(pic.ravel())
res.filepath_raw = out
res.file_format = "PNG"
res.save()
print("ok")

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block s1?>

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_figma flows; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use-figjam/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-diagram — MANDATORY before calling generate_diagram; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-diagram/SKILL.md
- /figma-design-to-code — MANDATORY before calling get_design_context; fallback: skill://figma/figma-design-to-code/SKILL.md

Extract fileKey and nodeId from Figma URLs:
- figma.com/design/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → convert "-" to ":" in nodeId

- figma.com/board/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → FigJam file, use get_figjam
- figma.com/slides/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Slides file
- figma.com/spec/:fileKey/:fileName?node-id=:nodeId → Figma Specs file, load the figma-spec skill and use use_figma

DESIGN-TO-CODE WORKFLOW (Figma → code):
MANDATORY: load the /figma-design-to-code skill BEFORE calling get_design_context — it carries the full workflow (adapting the reference, reusing existing project components and tokens, and honoring the response's hints by priority). After create_session, call get_design_context with the nodeId and fileKey — it is your primary tool; its output is a REFERENCE to adapt to the target project, not final code.

1. Load the /figma-generate-design skill if available.
2. Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session before any file tool; call create_new_file first if a new file is needed. Then ALWAYS call search_de… [truncated]

"""Ray-cast picture of a pose, three panels: texel colour, the side field, the kind of the verts.

Panel 3: red = raw head flag, green = in the band, blue = neither skin nor shirt (a face with one is not cut).
Verts made by the tie split or by the cut have no record: they show as 0.5 / grey.
  blender -b --python side_probe.py -- clips.blend debug.npz out.png Idle 17 front dx dy scale
"""
import math
import sys

import bpy
import numpy as np
from mathutils import Vector
from mathutils.interpolate import poly_3d_calc

path, dbg, out, clip, frame, view, dx, dy, scale = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:][:9]
dx, dy, scale = float(dx), float(dy), float(scale)
bpy.ops.wm.open_mainfile(filepath=path)
ob = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "MESH")
arm = next(o for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == "ARMATURE")
data = np.load(dbg)
side, head, band, shirt = data["side"], data["head"], data["band"], data["shirt"]
n = len(side)
if clip != "rest":
    action = bpy.data.actions[clip]
    if arm.animation_data is None:
        arm.animation_data_create()
    arm.animation_data.action = action
    if hasattr(arm.animation_data, "action_slot") and getattr(action, "slots", None):
        arm.animation_data.action_slot = action.slots[0]
    bpy.context.scene.frame_set(int(frame))
dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
ev = ob.evaluated_get(dg)
me = ev.data
img = next(nd.image for m in me.materials for nd in m.node_tree.nodes
           if nd.type == "TEX_IMAGE" and nd.image and nd.outputs[0].links
           and any(l.to_socket.name == "Base Color" for l in nd.outputs[0].links))
w, h = img.size
px = np.empty(w * h * 4, dtype=np.float32)
img.pixels.foreach_get(px)
px = px.reshape(h, w, 4)
uv = me.uv_layers.active.data
az = {"front": 0.0, "q3": 38.0, "q3r": -38.0, "side": 90.0}[view]
el = math.radians(8.0)
a = math.radians(az)
d = Vector((-math.sin(a) * math.cos(el), -math.cos(a) * math.cos(el), math.sin(el))).normalized()
right = Vector((0, 0, 1)).cross(d).normalized()
up = d.cross(right).normalized()
if up.z < 0:
    up = -up
if right.dot(Vector((math.cos(a), -math.sin(a), 0))) < 0:
    right = -right
target = arm.matrix_world @ arm.pose.bones["neck_01"].head + right * dx + up * dy
N = 560
pic = np.zeros((N, 3 * N, 4), dtype=np.float32)
pic[..., 3] = 1
for j in range(N):
    for i in range(N):
        o = target + d * 3.0 + right * ((i + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale + up * ((j + 0.5) / N - 0.5) * scale
        ok, loc, nor, fi = ev.ray_cast(o, -d)
        if not ok:
            continue
        f = me.polygons[fi]
        bw = poly_3d_calc([me.vertices[k].co for k in f.vertices], loc)
        c = sum((uv[l].uv * b for l, b in zip(f.loop_indices, bw)), Vector((0, 0)))
        pic[j, i, :3] = px[min(int(c.y % 1 * h), h - 1), min(int(c.x % 1 * w), w - 1), :3]
        s = sum((side[k] if k < n else 0.5) * b for k, b in zip(f.vertices, bw))
        edge = min(bw) < 0.03
        pic[j, N + i, :3] = (1.0, 0.6, 0.2) if abs(s - 0.5) < 0.02 else ((s * 0.8, s * 0.8, s * 0.8 + 0.2) if edge else (s, s, s))
        kind = np.zeros(3)
        for k, b in zip(f.vertices, bw):
            if k < n:
                kind += b * np.array((float(head[k]), float(band[k]), float(not (head[k] or shirt[k]))))
            else:
                kind += b * np.array((0.5, 0.5, 0.5))
        pic[j, 2 * N + i, :3] = kind * (0.7 if edge else 1.0)
res = bpy.data.images.new("ray", 3 * N, N)
res.pixels.foreach_set(pic.ravel())
res.filepath_raw = out
res.file_format = "PNG"
res.save()
print("ok")

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

Reach for this when the task matches an available agent type, when you have independent work to run in parallel, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate it and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps. For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. Once you've delegated a search, don't also run it yourself — wait for the result.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
